commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Apply each endpoint's top_logprobs cut in derender
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59513. Builds on the generate logprobs shape from #58181 (merged); rebased on main, one commit.

The engine's per-position logprobs hold the sampled token first and then ranks `1..k`, so `k` distinct entries when the sampled token is in the top `k` and `k + 1` when it is not. `/v1/chat/completions` keeps the first `k` and `/v1/completions` the first `k + 1` (the OpenAI completions convention). Generate cut to `max(k, 1)` and derender passed that through, so `/v1/completions/derender` returned `k` entries where the coupled endpoint returns `k + 1` whenever the sampled token was outside the top `k`. The greedy parity tests never produce that case. Following @shimib's suggestion on #58181:

- **Generate** (Python and Rust, both `output_mode`s) returns every candidate the engine produced, sampled first, with no cut. Rust drops the repeated sampled entry (its engine row lists a sampled top-1 token twice) by skipping later entries equal to the sampled token (linear, no allocation, even for `logprobs=-1`).
- **Derender** applies the coupled endpoint's cut through the same helpers the coupled endpoints now use (`chat_top_logprobs_limit` / `completion_top_logprobs_limit`), read from `chat_request` / `completion_request`: chat keeps entry `i` when `logprob_token_ids` is set, `top_logprobs == -1` or `i < top_logprobs` (`_get_top_logprobs`); completions when `logprob_token_ids` is set or `logprobs >= i`. The cut happens before decoding. Without the request derender returns every candidate (documented).
- **Rust `/v1/chat/completions`** drops the repeated sampled entry, like Python; before, a sampled top-1 token appeared twice and one candidate was lost.
- Docs: `renderer.md` (what generate returns) and `derenderer.md` (the per-endpoint cut).

## Test Plan

- New `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_logprobs_endpoint_parity.py`: engine dicts built with the engine's own `append_logprobs_for_next_position` and detokenized as the engine does, with the sampled token at rank 1, inside and outside the top `k`, run through the real coupled chat / completions helpers and through generate + derender; `k` in 0, 1, 2, 5 (and -1 for chat). Plus: without the request, every candidate is kept.
- Updated generate unit tests to engine-realistic dicts; Rust tests for the generate dedup (no cut) and the chat dedup.
- End-to-end on a live server (`--enable-scale-out`, Qwen3-4B, L20): the same request (`temperature=1.5`, seeds 7/11/23, `k` = 1/2/5, 96 tokens) through the coupled endpoint and through render -> `/inference/v1/generate` -> derender, compared per position (token ids, `top_logprobs` length, tokens, bytes, logprobs within 1e-4), before and after this change.
- Benchmark of generate and derender cost at `top_logprobs=20`.

## Test Result

End-to-end, 18 trials (9 chat, 9 completions), 1,632 comparable positions:

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| positions where generate + derender differs from the coupled endpoint | 215 | **0** |
| of which the sampled token was outside the top `k` | 215 | 0 |
| chat positions that differ | 0 | 0 |

Before the change the mismatches were exactly the 215 completions positions with the sampled token outside the top `k`. One chat trial is excluded on both sides because the coupled endpoint itself is not run-to-run deterministic there (two identical coupled requests diverge at position 73 once the prefix is cached, at `temperature=1.5`); generate is repeatable.

Benchmark (1,000 positions, `top_logprobs=20`, 30% of positions with the sampled token outside the top `k`, Qwen2.5 tokenizer, median of 7):

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| generate `_create_tokens_logprobs` | 14.8 µs/token | 13.5 µs/token |
| generate response size | 1,043 B/token | 1,057 B/token |
| chat derender | 66.2 µs/token | 65.2 µs/token |
| completions derender | 67.4 µs/token | 69.3 µs/token (decodes the entry it used to drop) |

Tests on an L20 with live servers (tiny Llama, gpt2, Qwen3-0.6B): `test_derender.py` 27, `test_derender_stream.py` 52, `test_logprobs_endpoint_parity.py` 10, `test_generate_logprobs_conversion.py` 5, `test_serving_tokens.py` 13, `test_generate_stream.py` 31, `test_tokens_logprobs.py` 7 passed; not run there: the DeepSeek parser and gpt-oss harmony tests (model size) and the LoRA test (adapters not downloaded). CPU-only runs: 414 passed across `scale_out`, `test_serving_chat.py` and `openai/completion` (3 failures that fail identically on main). Rust: `vllm-server` 440 passed, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean. mypy (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12`) reports only the 2 existing `Parser` errors in `online_derenderer.py` that main has too; ruff and typos clean.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Pad fp16/bf16 GEMM weight row stride for L2 cache
commits.pr_body:
On gfx11 (RDNA3/3.5) a dense GEMM whose weight row stride is a multiple of 2048 bytes collide on the L2/MALL hashes, costing a large share of achievable bandwidth. Offsetting the row stride by one 128 B cache line dodges the collision.
This PR improves TTFT by up to 13% and TPOT by up to 3%.

We pad the row stride once in `UnquantizedLinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading`.
It has a minimal impact on memory consumption on affected layers only (1.29 % of weight memory for Qwen3-8B: 171 MiB on 12.94 GiB).

The predicate is `(K * element_size) % 2048 == 0`, so for bf16/fp16 it fires on any layer
with `K % 1024 == 0`. That covers most of the Llama/Qwen dense family: for Qwen3-8B all
four linears qualify (`qkv`/`o`/`gate_up` `K=4096` → 8192 B, `down` `K=12288` → 24576 B).

Gated on gfx11. This might also apply to gfx12, but we will need to measure and can enable as a follow up.

## Benchmark

On AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151),
`--num-prompts 5`, 2 interleaved reps per cell. Before/after this PR.

| Model (in/out len) | Qualifying | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | Weight memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-8B` 1920/128 | 100 % | 918.02 → 852.39 ms (**−7.15 %**) | 72.15 → 69.83 ms (**−3.21 %**) | 15.27 → 15.47 GiB |
| `Qwen3-8B` 128/128 | 100 % | 119.35 → 103.59 ms (**−13.20 %**) | 70.50 → 68.11 ms (**−3.39 %**) | 15.27 → 15.47 GiB |
| `Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` 1920/128 | 70.7 % | 969.01 → 932.10 ms (**−3.81 %**) | 30.37 → 29.36 ms (**−3.33 %**) | 7.16 → 7.27 GiB |
| `Qwen3-4B` 1920/128 | 10.4 % | 512.12 → 510.49 ms (not resolvable) | 38.85 → 38.03 ms (**−2.11 %**) | 7.56 → 7.57 GiB |
| `Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct` 1920/128 | 0 % | 198.34 → 201.03 ms (no effect) | 14.64 → 14.74 ms (no effect) | 2.89 → 2.89 GiB |

## Accuracy

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, full 1319-question test set, 5-shot, greedy
(temperature 0.0, seed 42), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` on gfx1151:

| | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| padding off | 88.931 % | 1173 / 1319 | 0.0 |
| padding on | 89.159 % | 1176 / 1319 | 0.0 |

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this PR. Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, and
all tests, benchmarks and evals listed above were run on the hardware named.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Keep routing rows during DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Keep every prefill routing row when DeepSeek V4.1 decoder replay runs with returned routed experts enabled. Extracted from #61388 as a standalone fix based on `main`.

## Claims

- R3 requests use the existing prompt-logprobs keep-row mechanism so decoder replay does not omit their routing computations.
- Cover eager and PIECEWISE replay in the existing replay-batch suite.
- The diff contains the request row-retention policy and its regression coverage in two files.

## Validation

- **20 isolated CPU policy cases passed** using the actual request-admission, graph-selection, and replay row-selection methods with real CPU tensors. The same checks against unmodified `main` reproduce **6 failures / 14 passes**, including a 300-row prefill incorrectly reduced to 128 rows.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering, and `git diff --check`: passed with local UTF-8/Git Bash interpreter adaptations.
- The pre-split #61388 validation recorded real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1 TP1/DP2/EP, 300/301-token prefill: late layers previously executed only 128 rows; the keep-row fix retained all rows in all 40 layers. The request-retention change is preserved from that combined revision.

GPU/model runs were not repeated for the split. CPU checks stop at the row-selection boundary and substitute configuration/base-state/input-gather fixtures; they do not validate CUDA kernels or attention numerics. The GPU regression remains in the existing CI-tethered suite:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py
```

## Details

Decoder replay can normally skip older prefill rows when only final logits are needed. Returned routing needs every accepted token's decisions; scattering the remaining rows cannot recover computations that never ran. Mark R3 requests as requiring every row when admitted, using the existing keep-row policy.

R3-enabled replay therefore retains prefill work that could otherwise be trimmed. No throughput measurement is claimed.

Duplicate-work checks refreshed open PR searches for `61388 in:body`, routed-expert capture, and decoder replay. #52902 adds API consistency tests, #57184 handles DBO staging/offsets, and #56778 implements terminal transport; they do not implement this NVIDIA V4.1 admission policy. The same fix has been removed from #61388, so this is its single review location.

AI assistance was used to split and validate the existing fix.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Engage indexer TP row sharding on total rows, not per-rank rows
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

> This PR description was written by @ZJY0516.

## Overview

Follow-up to #54951, addressing https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54951#discussion_r4267244007: gate the sparse-indexer TP row sharding on **total** scheduled prefill rows instead of per-rank rows, so the 8xH100 TP8 recipe can actually engage it. The floor becomes `AttentionConfig.indexer_tp_shard_min_rows` (default 65536).

Not a duplicate: no other open PR changes how this floor scales with TP. #60601 lowers the same floor on ROCm only; whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Claims

- TP8 engages row sharding at `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`; before, it needed 131072, which OOMs on 80 GB Hopper.
- −34.1% mean TTFT on a 1.02M-token prompt at TP8 under an H100-equivalent memory budget.
- TP4 engagement point unchanged (64K total rows). TP2 moves from 32K to 64K total rows by design.
- The floor is configurable, e.g. `-ac '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows": 131072}'`.

## Validation

**Problem reproduced** on 8xH200 with an 80 GB-equivalent budget (`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.56`, TP8, BF16 KV, merged-commit build `3e8e1364`):

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 131072` | engine init fails: `Available KV cache memory: -6.94 GiB` |
| `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536` | server healthy, but a 70K-token request schedules `num_rows=65536 < threshold=131072` on every chunk → **0 engagements** |

**TTFT at the H100 budget** (8xH200, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.568` ≈ 81,662 MiB/card vs H100's 81,559 MiB), TP8, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, FP8 KV, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, streaming completions with one request in flight; only the floor differs between arms:

| Prompt | row-sharded (default) | replicated (floor = 2,000,000) | Δ mean TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.02M tok (n=2) | **31.57 s** | 47.92 s | **−34.1%** |

The replicated arm was measured with an earlier revision's `VLLM_INDEXER_TP_SHARD_MIN_ROWS=2000000`; the equivalent now is `-ac '{"indexer_tp_shard_min_rows": 2000000}'`. The gain grows with context depth (0.48 s saved at 255K vs 16.35 s at 1.02M): per-row indexer cost ramps with causal depth while the per-row exchange cost stays constant.

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py`: 12 passed (TP8 parametrization, total-not-per-rank floor, TP2 32K–64K window stays replicated, floor never below `tp_size`).
- End-to-end serve + long-context completions on TP8 at the H100-equivalent budget; engagement verified via NCCL coll logging, outputs sane.

## Details

Per rank, the saved replicated indexer work (`~ (1 - 1/tp) * rows`) and the `all_gatherv` index traffic (`~ (tp - 1)/tp * rows * topk * 4B`) both scale with `(tp - 1)/tp`, so the engagement crossover in total rows is tp-independent to first order. The old per-rank floor grew the total requirement linearly with `tp`. 65536 is the TP4-calibrated total floor from #54951.

- TP2 now engages later (64K instead of 32K total rows); the exchange's fixed latency term is largest at small `tp`.
- `balanced_prefill_row_shard` takes the floor as an argument and clamps it to at least `tp_size`, so every rank always gets at least one row.
- The floor was calibrated on H200 with NVSwitch; other interconnects were not measured. Startup auto-calibration is a possible follow-up.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Report the real cause when the worker outgrows its memory reservation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59471.

When the CPU worker's own footprint (model weights plus runtime) exceeds the memory reserved by `--gpu-memory-utilization`, `CPUWorker.determine_available_memory` computes a negative KV cache budget. That case shared the "available < requested" error, which printed the negative size and told users to reduce memory used by other processes, the opposite of the fix:

```
ValueError: Available memory on node 0 (1.34/8.0 GiB) on kv cache allocation is less than requested memory for kv (-0.6/0.16 GiB). Reduce CPU memory used by other processes.
```

This PR splits the two conditions:

- **Worker outgrew its reservation** (`requested_memory_for_kv <= 0`): a new error states the footprint and the reservation, and points to what actually works. That is a larger `--gpu-memory-utilization`, with the smallest fraction that could fit, or an explicit `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` / `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`. The wording follows #42479's CPU messages.
- **Node short of free memory** (`requested_memory_for_kv > available_memory`): the existing error is unchanged.

Only the error path changes. When the budget fits, sizing and startup behave exactly as before, and nothing runs after startup.

**Not a duplicate.** No open issue or PR covers this branch. #42479 reworded the neighbouring CPU memory errors (the startup check in this file, and two in `kv_cache_utils.py`) but not this one. Among open PRs touching `cpu_worker.py`, #51876 changes only `__init__`, with no overlap.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py`, CPU-only, no model. It covers three cases:
  - the worker outgrew its reservation: the new error with the right remedy, no negative size and no "other processes" advice;
  - the node is short of memory: the existing message still fires;
  - the budget fits: the KV size equals the reservation minus the footprint.
- Real engine on the CPU backend: `LLM(model="HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M", dtype="float32", gpu_memory_utilization=0.02)` on `main` and on this branch.

## Test Result

Unit tests, this branch:
```
PASSED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_footprint_above_reservation_asks_for_a_larger_reservation
PASSED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_short_node_memory_still_asks_to_free_memory
PASSED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_budget_that_fits_sizes_the_kv_cache
3 passed
```
The same file against unmodified `main`: only the first test fails, so the other two paths are untouched.
```
FAILED tests/v1/worker/test_cpu_worker_kv_budget.py::test_footprint_above_reservation_asks_for_a_larger_reservation
1 failed, 2 passed
```

Real engine (macOS 27.0, Apple M1, 8 GiB, CPU backend built from `main` `fc2c801ad9`), `gpu_memory_utilization=0.02`:

- `main`:
  ```
  ValueError: Available memory on node 0 (1.34/8.0 GiB) on kv cache allocation is less than requested memory for kv (-0.6/0.16 GiB). Reduce CPU memory used by other processes.
  ```
- this branch:
  ```
  ValueError: The worker already uses 0.64 GiB (model weights and runtime), more than the 0.16 GiB of CPU memory reserved for it on node 0, leaving none for the KV cache. On the CPU backend, the `--gpu-memory-utilization` flag controls the fraction of CPU memory reserved (despite its name). To resolve: increase `--gpu-memory-utilization` to more than 0.09, or set the KV cache size explicitly with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` or VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE.
  ```

Separately observed, and identical with and without this change: on this machine the engine process sometimes does not exit after this worker startup error (2/2 runs on each side hung past a 240 s timeout; an earlier run on `main` exited promptly). This PR does not touch shutdown.

`pre-commit` on both files: ruff check and format, typos, mypy, SPDX and the remaining hooks passed. `check-test-tethering` and `check-root-lazy-imports` also pass when run with Python 3.12. The new test sits in `tests/v1/worker/`, which the `v1-executor-worker` job runs as a directory.

No model evaluation: the change only affects an error raised before the engine starts, so no model output changes.

---

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Leave the final stop token out of chat derender text
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Partially fixes #57052: the chat token-stop part (EOS and `stop_token_ids`). Completion derender and stop strings remain open there.

Chat derender now leaves the stop token that finished generation out of the decoded text, the way the engine's detokenizer does. This fixes `test_parity_reasoning` and `test_stream_parity_reasoning` in `(H200 MIG 35GB) Entrypoints Integration (API Server)`, which fail on main because derender returns `...\boxed{391}\n\]<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` where the coupled server returns `...\boxed{391}\n\]`. Examples: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95020#01a13dbe-64d7-4310-bfe8-807fb58fd14b (batch) and https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94727#01a13986-c733-4d38-ad14-feb389277a93 (stream).

## Claims

- Chat derender (batch, plain stream and parser stream) no longer puts the EOS / stop-token text into `content` when `finish_reason` is `stop`. This matches the coupled `/v1/chat/completions` output.
- `include_stop_str_in_output=true` still keeps it, and `ignore_eos` turns off the EOS check, both as in the engine.
- The returned `token_ids` and the ids passed to the parser are unchanged and still include the stop token, as on the coupled path.

## Validation

All runs used the CI image for main `10d2c6083d` (the failing build 95020) on an H200:

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| new `test_parsed_derender_leaves_out_stop_token_like_engine` (EOS, `stop_token_ids`, stop string, `include_stop_str_in_output`) | **fails** on the EOS and `stop_token_ids` cases | passes |
| `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py` (non-server tests) | 94 passed, 1 failed (the new test) | 95 passed |
| `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py` (GPU, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B) | fails intermittently on main CI | 10 passed, 6 skipped |

## Details

**Root cause.** When generation stops on a stop token, the engine's `IncrementalDetokenizer.update` drops that token before decoding unless `include_stop_str_in_output` is set (`vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py`). Derender received the same `token_ids`, including the stop token, and decoded all of them. Without a parser this was hidden, because `skip_special_tokens=True` drops the EOS anyway. With a reasoning or tool parser, derender decodes with `skip_special_tokens=False` so the parser can see its markers, and the EOS text ends up in `content`. Each test fails only on runs whose greedy, 256-token generation ends on EOS rather than at the length limit. On main that is a minority of runs, so it looks like a flake.

**Fix.** `_text_token_ids` follows the engine's `stop_terminated` using the choice's `stop_reason` (passed through since #60251): `finish_reason == "stop"` with a non-string `stop_reason` means a token stopped generation. `None` means EOS and an int means a `stop_token_ids` entry. A string `stop_reason` (stop string) never drops a token, and neither does `include_stop_str_in_output`. As a guard, because `finish_reason` defaults to `"stop"` when a client sends neither field, the last id must actually be that stop token: equal to the int `stop_reason`, or one of the model's EOS ids (tokenizer and `generation_config`) when it is `None`. This applies at the three chat decode sites only; the ids returned to the client and to the parser are untouched.

**Relation to #59510.** #59510 (@pOpO1-9, "Hide stop text on batch derender") proposes similar helpers, aimed mainly at batch derender plus stop strings. It has had no review since Oct 7 and now conflicts with main. This PR is the minimal fix for the chat paths that are failing on main today. Completion derender and stop strings are left to #59510. If a reviewer prefers to land #59510 instead, this can be closed.

Not a duplicate otherwise: I searched open PRs for derender EOS, stop-token and `test_parity_reasoning` fixes; #59510 is the only related one.

commits.pr_title: [MM][CG] Support ViT full CUDA graph for DeepSeek-VL2
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Support ViT full CUDA graph capture/replay for DeepSeek-VL2, as tracked in #38175.

Previously, `DeepseekVLV2ForCausalLM` ran vision encoding (SigLIP ViT + MLP
projector) eagerly on every forward pass, incurring repeated CPU kernel-dispatch
overhead. This PR implements the `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` protocol so
`EncoderCudaGraphManager` can capture the ViT + projector forward pass once and
replay it, eliminating that overhead for batches that fit within a captured
budget.

**Key design decisions:**
- `encoder_cudagraph_forward` returns raw per-tile projector output
  `[N_tiles, hw, D]`; newline tokens and the view-separator are reattached in
  `postprocess_encoder_output` (outside the graph), keeping the captured
  computation simple and shape-static.
- `encoder_eager_forward` calls the existing `_pixel_values_to_embedding` and
  returns a flat `[total_tokens, D]` tensor, matching what `scatter_output_slices`
  expects in the eager-fallback path.
- `_proj_hw()` derives projector output spatial size from config
  (`ceil((image_size // patch_size) / downsample_ratio)`), consistent with the
  token-count formula in `DeepseekVL2ProcessingInfo.get_num_image_tokens`.

## Test Plan

**Unit test:**
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py \
    -v -k "DeepseekVL2"

# Full suite to confirm no regression
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -v
```

**Functional test:**
```bash
# Enable encoder CUDA graph via compilation_config in run_deepseek_vl2()
python examples/generate/multimodal/vision_language_offline.py \
    -m deepseek_vl_v2 --modality image
```

**Benchmark:**

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Disambiguate ROCm attention class names
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This is a small, focused naming cleanup of DeepSeek V4.1 ROCm attention classes and their selector. It preserves runtime behavior and compatibility with existing configurations.

DeepSeek V4.1 ROCm attention defined its own SWA metadata, SWA metadata builder, and sparse-MLA backend under the same class names as the DeepSeek V4 ROCm implementations. The ROCm SWA metadata builder is a distinct type. It subclasses `DeepseekV41SparseSWAMetadataBuilder`, which handles V4.1's 0/1/2 compression topology.

Rename those V4.1-local classes so they cannot be confused with `vllm.models.deepseek_v4.amd.rocm`:

- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadata`
- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder`
- `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend`

`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` now uses the renamed sparse-MLA backend, while its SWA backend returns the renamed metadata builder. The canonical V4.1 selector is `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`; V4.1 continues to accept `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` as a legacy alias for backward compatibility. DeepSeek V4 behavior is unchanged.

## Test Plan

- `git diff --check`
- Changed-file pre-commit
- Focused registry and backend-selection tests
- Start `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` with TP=4 using both `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` and `ROCM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, and send a completion request to each server.

## Test Result

- Changed-file pre-commit passed (ruff, mypy 3.10–3.13, SPDX, test tethering).
- Focused tests passed for the distinct V4/V4.1 registry paths and for selecting the V4.1 implementation through both the legacy and canonical selectors.
- TP=4 serve smokes passed on four MI355X GPUs with both selectors. Each server returned HTTP 200 and generated `42` for the completion request.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Terminate streaming sessions on ABORT/ERROR and prevent zombie sessions
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Split out from #53861 (bugs 2 and 3 of the 4 streaming-input session lifecycle fixes there), with the original author included as co-author — this is a carve-out for independent review/merge, not duplicate work. Bugs 1 (collector merging across chunk boundaries) and 4 (zero-chunk streams / DP sticky routing) are being split separately.

**Bug 2 — engine-side ABORT/ERROR treated as a normal chunk boundary.** `OutputProcessor.process_outputs` treated any `finish_reason` on a streaming-input request as "chunk done, wait for next chunk". ABORT and ERROR end the whole session, so treating them as a chunk boundary left `generate()` waiting forever and desynced the frontend/scheduler chunk queues. Fix: only non-terminal finish reasons are chunk boundaries (`streaming_chunk_boundary`); ABORT/ERROR finish the request state and also send an abort back to the engine (see below).

**Bug 3 — a chunk sent after the session finished resurrects it as a zombie.** If a chunk ADD reaches the engine after the session was aborted/finished, the scheduler sees an unknown resumable id and admits it as a new session. That session then sits in `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` forever, holding KV blocks, with no frontend state left to abort it. Fix (reworked per review, no new request fields):
- `handle_inputs` checks `output_processor.has_request()` before each non-first chunk and before the final empty request, and stops if the session is gone. There is no `await` between this check and the ADD send, and `AsyncLLM.abort()` removes frontend state before sending ABORT on the same socket, so any chunk that passes the check is ordered before the abort. This holds for every abort path, including direct `abort()` calls (e.g. realtime `cleanup()`).
- For the engine-finished race (engine finishes the session with ABORT/ERROR while a chunk sent before the frontend saw that finish is in flight), the output processor always re-sends an abort for a terminally-finished streaming session. That abort is ordered after any such chunk, so a re-created session is cleaned up.
- `DPLBAsyncMPClient.abort_requests_async` broadcasts aborts for ids with no routing entry to all engines, since the routing entry is dropped when the engine reports the request finished.

## Test Plan

```
ruff check / ruff format --check (ruff 0.14.0) on changed files
pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_async_llm_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k "streaming or abort or chunk"
```

New coverage: `test_streaming_input_stop_is_chunk_boundary`, `test_streaming_input_abort_error_is_terminal[abort|error]` (bug 2); `test_handle_inputs_stops_after_session_finished[True|False]`, `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines[1|2]` (bug 3).

## Test Result

- ruff check / format: pass.
- On macOS CPU: all streaming-input and output-processor tests above pass. `test_abort_requests[*]` errors only because the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` tokenizer cannot be downloaded here (same on main).
- `test_engine_core_client.py` is skipped on non-CUDA platforms, so `test_dplb_abort_of_finished_request_goes_to_all_engines` was run standalone: it passes with this change and fails against the previous `abort_requests_async`.
- Not yet validated end-to-end against a realtime model on GPU.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (split and adaptation onto latest main). The bug-3 approach was reworked following @njhill's review suggestion. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

Co-authored-by: Benedikt Falk <bfalk@nvidia.com>

commits.pr_title: [Model] Support every Decision 3.0 size (d3-flash, d3-mini, d3-nano, d3-lite, d3-edge)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make every Decision 3.0 model work in vLLM: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-nano` stopped while loading weights, and d3-flash, d3-lite, d3-mini and d3-edge had no published validation on current vLLM. Follow-up to #61565, which added Decision 3.0 and validated d3, d3-mini and d3-edge; its "Follow-ups" section promised this PR.

## Claims

- **d3-nano loads.** Its checkpoint has one `model.safetensors` and no weight index, so the default loader also read `readout.safetensors` as a backbone file and stopped with `ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'weight' in D3ForSequenceClassification`. `D3ForSequenceClassification` now names the readout's only tensor in `is_unused_checkpoint_weight`, so the backbone pass skips that file; the readout still loads as the FP32 `score` head through `secondary_weights`.
- **All five sizes give the checkpoint runtime's decisions** with `vllm serve vllm-sr/<model>` and no flags, on one AMD Instinct MI300X: 0 to 2 of 416 decisions changed per model, all near-ties (the reference's two most likely answers within 0.015 of each other), with a median probability difference of 0.003 (table below).
- **Throughput.** At 8 and 64 closed-loop clients vLLM serves 2.0x to 3.6x the requests per second of the checkpoint's own server on the mixed text / image / video load; one request at a time it is 7 % to 32 % slower (each question is its own engine request).
- The docs list all six models, the GPU test runs d3-nano next to d3-edge, and the test registry lists every size.

## Validation

**Setup**: one AMD Instinct MI300X (ROCm 7.2), a new `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.3-complete` container with empty caches. vLLM is the ROCm nightly wheel `0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82` (it contains #61565, and every file on the Decision 3.0 path is identical to `main`) with this PR's `d3.py` copied over the installed one; no kernels were built. The reference is the checkpoint's own runtime, `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`, with the versions its `requirements.txt` pins (torch 2.13.0+rocm7.1, transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2), in its own venv on the same GPU. Checkpoints at their current `main`: `vllm-sr/d3-edge` @ cab71e6a, `vllm-sr/d3-lite` @ 9c107031, `vllm-sr/d3-nano` @ aeb70d4d, `vllm-sr/d3-mini` @ 97dd054d, `vllm-sr/d3-flash` @ 8b35c853.

**Reproducer**: in the same container, the unchanged nightly fails on d3-nano and this PR loads it:

```bash
vllm serve vllm-sr/d3-nano
# nightly 0.32.0rc1.dev190+g3f1bcfd82:
#   ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'weight' in D3ForSequenceClassification
# with this PR: ready, and the agreement set below
```

**Answers vs the reference**: the same 416 questions as #61565 (3 states x 128 typed questions, 1-, 4- and 16-question text, a 4-question JSON state, a 40-option choice, an image with 1 and 4 questions, and a 10 s 1080p video). The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Model | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max | Image / video questions, max abs dp |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| d3-edge (0.59B) | 0 / 416 | 0.0030 | 0.0122 | 0.034 | 0.0071 |
| d3-lite (0.85B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0149) | 0.0031 | 0.0097 | 0.022 | 0.0182 |
| d3-nano (2.21B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0028) | 0.0028 | 0.0094 | 0.030 | 0.0300 |
| d3-mini (4.54B) | 1 / 416 (reference margin 0.0042) | 0.0028 | 0.0076 | 0.042 | 0.0192 |
| d3-flash (8.39B) | 2 / 416 (reference margins 0.0128, 0.0077) | 0.0027 | 0.0077 | 0.020 | 0.0104 |

**Throughput**: closed loop, 20 s per level after an 8 s warm-up, over the mix of #61565 (40 % one-question text, 20 % four-question text, 10 % four-question JSON, 10 % 40-option choice, 15 % new 1.6 MP image, 5 % new 10 s 1080p video; every image and video carries new bytes). The checkpoint server is the package's `d3_server.py` (AutoModel behind HTTP). Each cell gives req/s and p50 / p90 latency in ms:

| Model | Side | 1 client | 8 clients | 64 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3-edge | checkpoint server | 18.7 (12 / 89) | 36.5 (187 / 341) | 26.9 (2,108 / 2,569) |
| d3-edge | vLLM | 16.1 (17 / 85) | 72.0 (34 / 302) | 61.5 (36 / 4,233) |
| d3-lite | checkpoint server | 15.9 (25 / 102) | 24.6 (285 / 457) | 19.2 (2,863 / 3,104) |
| d3-lite | vLLM | 10.8 (36 / 107) | 59.7 (81 / 229) | 59.5 (94 / 4,213) |
| d3-nano | checkpoint server | 14.2 (26 / 125) | 20.7 (358 / 521) | 16.5 (3,192 / 3,677) |
| d3-nano | vLLM | 11.1 (32 / 113) | 52.8 (94 / 254) | 59.8 (235 / 3,699) |
| d3-mini | checkpoint server | 11.4 (33 / 147) | 16.2 (449 / 671) | 12.7 (3,953 / 4,276) |
| d3-mini | vLLM | 10.4 (32 / 135) | 37.1 (167 / 360) | 35.7 (1,585 / 2,031) |
| d3-flash | checkpoint server | 10.7 (34 / 203) | 11.2 (698 / 934) | 9.3 (5,126 / 5,480) |
| d3-flash | vLLM | 9.9 (32 / 169) | 24.6 (297 / 485) | 20.8 (2,706 / 3,130) |

**Start-up**: vLLM's launch to the first answer from empty caches, the model download included: 132 to 172 s (d3-edge 140 s, d3-lite 136 s, d3-nano 132 s, d3-mini 163 s, d3-flash 172 s).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py` (MI300X, this PR): `[vllm-sr/d3-edge]` PASSED, `[vllm-sr/d3-nano]` PASSED (2 passed in 270 s). Without this PR, d3-nano fails at load as in the reproducer.
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py tests/models/test_registry.py tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_strategies.py -k "decision_config or joint_head or D3 or d3 or strategy_selection"` (MI300X, this PR): 13 passed.
- CPU check of `DefaultModelLoader.get_all_weights` on a d3-nano-like layout (`model.safetensors` with backbone tensors plus `readout.safetensors`, no index): on main the backbone pass yields the readout's root `weight`; with this PR it yields only the backbone tensors, and `score.weight` still comes from `secondary_weights`.
- vLLM CI on NVIDIA, Buildkite #95083 (H200, MIG 18 GB, the multimodal pooling step): `test_d3.py` `[vllm-sr/d3-edge]` and `[vllm-sr/d3-nano]` PASSED; the d3-nano run logs `Skipped 1/2 safetensors shard(s) holding no weights the model loads`.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass (actionlint skipped locally; no workflow files changed).

## Details

- **Root cause**: without `model.safetensors.index.json`, `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` keeps every `*.safetensors` file of the repo (`filter_duplicate_safetensors_files` returns them all when the index is missing), so `readout.safetensors` ({`weight`: [255, hidden]}) joins the backbone pass. Its root key `weight` matches no module, and `AutoWeightsLoader` raises. The other five checkpoints ship an index that lists only the backbone shards, so the index filter already drops the readout there. d3-nano is the only Decision 3.0 repo without an index.
- **Fix**: `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` is the existing hook the default loader passes to `filter_safetensors_files_by_weight_name` for the primary weights only; it drops a safetensors file when every tensor in it is unused. The readout file holds a single tensor named `weight`, which no backbone checkpoint has at the root. Its own `secondary_weights` source sets no such rule and keeps loading it under the `score.` prefix. For indexed checkpoints nothing changes beyond reading the shard headers, which the loader already does for pooling models (their protocol default returns False).
- **Alternatives considered**: `allow_patterns_overrides=["model*.safetensors"]` would also skip the index filter and depend on file names; adding an index to the Hub repo fixes only that copy of the checkpoint.
- **CI**: `test_d3.py` runs in the optional "Multimodal Models (Extended Pooling)" step; d3-nano adds a 4.5 GB checkpoint there. d3-lite, d3-mini and d3-flash take the same code path as d3-edge and d3-nano and are covered by the measurements above rather than CI, to keep the step's downloads and run time small.
- **Not measured**: agreement and throughput on NVIDIA GPUs (only the CI test above ran there; no NVIDIA GPU was available to me), tensor parallelism, LoRA.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers d3-nano or the other sizes (searched for Decision 3.0, `vllm-sr/d3`, d3-nano, `D3ForSequenceClassification`, `decision_config`); #61565 is merged.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Create cuBLAS handles before memory profiling to avoid OOM
commits.pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/199944
Purpose
On small GPUs (e.g. an H200 35GB MIG slice), engine startup can fail during the memory profiling run with:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate(handle)`
```
This was seen in tests/v1/e2e/general/test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill.py with google/gemma-3n-E2B-it on torch 2.14.1 and the 2.15.0 RC (pytorch/pytorch#199944).

### Root cause

cuBLAS(Lt) asks CUDA for its handle memory directly. When torch's own cudaMalloc fails, torch frees its unused cache and retries, but a cuBLAS request never triggers that because torch doesn't see it. Profiling can grow torch's cache until the GPU is full, and the first cuBLAS call then fails even though torch holds idle memory it could have given back.
In this case:

- Loading weights does no matmuls, so the first cuBLAS call in the process happens inside profile_run, at the gemma3n vision projection. That call creates the handle.
- By then, torch had reserved 29.5 GiB, while live tensors peaked at 21.9 GiB. That left 0.04 GiB free on the device, and cublasCreate failed with about 19 GiB sitting unused in torch's cache.
- The scoped max_split_size_mb:20 from #58430 makes this more likely, adding about 2.9 GiB of reserved memory during profiling.

### Fix

Create the handles while memory is still free. At the start of Worker.determine_available_memory, call torch.cuda.current_blas_handle() and run one tiny linear with a bias, which also sets up cuBLASLt. Every GEMM during profiling then reuses the existing handles, so profiling needs no allocations outside torch's allocator.

The handles are created after init_snapshot, so their memory is still counted in total_consumed and comes out of the KV-cache budget as before. In the repro the KV cache was about 0.1 GiB smaller, which is the handle cost.

### Test Result

Without fix (2 runs) | FAIL ×2, CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED | 29.52 / 0.04 GiB
With fix (4 runs) | PASS ×4 | 29.43 / 0.07 GiB

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Emit kv/ec transfer params at the top level of render output
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python render now puts `kv_transfer_params` and `ec_transfer_params` at the top level of the generate request on every route, instead of leaving them in `sampling_params.extra_args`. 

## Claims

- Chat and completions render emit the transfer params as top-level fields, the same as responses render
- `sampling_params.extra_args` no longer carries `kv_transfer_params` / `ec_transfer_params` on any render route
- Python render → Rust generate keeps the KV params. Before, P/D quietly recomputed the prompt

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -v
```

Added tests:
- Chat render: both params at the top level, `extra_args == {"foo": 1}` and the request's own `vllm_xargs` untouched
- Completions with two prompts: each generate request carries both params with no `extra_args`
- The existing responses test now also checks that `extra_args` is empty

## Details

Chat and completions only got the params through `to_sampling_params` which puts them in `extra_args`. Responses render sent them in both places. Rust generate never reads `extra_args`. It merges the top-level fields into `vllm_xargs`, so a Python render in front of a Rust generate lost the KV params with no error.

Leaving a copy in `extra_args` is also a trap. If a router clears the top-level block to turn P/D off, Python generate only copies non `None` values back, so the stale `extra_args` copy would still reach the engine.

The fix is a small helper `_hoist_transfer_params`. It copies `extra_args` before popping because `to_sampling_params ` aliases `request.vllm_xargs`. Python generate copies the top-level values back into `extra_args` for the engine, so engine behavior doesn't change.

One observable change. Anything reading `sampling_params.extra_args.kv_transfer_params` from render output won't find it there anymore. I am unaware of any such client doing this. llm-d's coordinator doesn't read it. `vllm_xargs` can't carry a dict value, so stripping these keys can't remove anything a client put there.

Not a duplicate.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4] AITER MegaMoE Fixed-Slot Dispatch For DeepSeek-V4
commits.pr_body:
AITER MegaMoEV2 (initially integrated in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59685) has two dispatch schemes:
1. Compact: a separate megamoe_prepare_compact kernel packs tokens before dispatch.
2. Fixed-slot: each token writes straight into a per-rank slot, with no prepare kernel.

AITER takes fixed-slot only when the runtime's max_tok_per_rank is at most FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR. That limit is 255 by default and can be raised with AITER_MEGA_FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR. In the initial integration, we built a single runtime with the compact path, so decode always pays for the compact prepare step.

This PR builds a second runtime and picks between the two paths at each decode step.

The decode runtime is sized `max_tok_per_rank = prev_power_of_2(FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR)`, which ends up being 128 by default. It's only built when AITER's bundle plan says that size actually uses fixed-slot. Otherwise behavior is unchanged. The fused shared expert makes 49 experts per rank, so no decode runtime is built with FSE enabled.

### Perf and Accuracy

#### Without MTP
| Concurrency | Tokens/rank/step | main TPOT p50 | This PR TPOT p50 | main tok/s | This PR tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 4 (fixed-slot) | 40.1 ms | **34.5 ms (−14%)** | 775 | **894 (+15%)** |
| 128 | 16 (fixed-slot) | 49.1 ms | **43.3 ms (−12%)** | 2490 | **2827 (+14%)** |
| 2048 | 256 (compact) | 121.3 ms | 121.9 ms | 14456 | 13934 |
#### With MTP (DSpark, 3 draft tokens)
| Concurrency | Tokens/rank/step | main TPOT p50 | This PR TPOT p50 | main ITL p50 | This PR ITL p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 16 (fixed-slot) | 15.4 ms | **14.0 ms (−9%)** | 50.6 ms | **44.9 ms (−11%)** |
| 128 | 64 (fixed-slot) | 23.0 ms | **22.0 ms (−4%)** | 67.6 ms | **58.1 ms (−14%)** |
| 512 | 256 (compact) | 45.8 ms | 45.5 ms | 113.9 ms | 113.7 ms |

At 2048 without MTP and 512 with MTP, both builds use the compact runtime, so they run the same kernels. So it is expected that there is no diff from the current main.
### Accuracy (gsm8k 5-shot, flexible / strict, ±0.006)
| | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Without MTP | 0.9530 / 0.9538 | 0.9545 / 0.9538 |
| With MTP | 0.9538 / 0.9538 | 0.9515 / 0.9515 |

MTP acceptance rate is 91–92% on both.

**Edit**: A useful note from @benenzhu 
>One note from that setup: with K6 drafts each decode request carries 7 tokens, so at concurrency 128 a rank holds 112+ tokens per step, about 143 on average in our runs because of uneven load. With the default FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR=255 the decode runtime holds 128 tokens, and those steps fall back to the compact path. We ran with AITER_MEGA_FIXED_SLOT_MAX_MTPR=511, which gives a 256-token decode runtime. It may be worth mentioning this knob in the description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Always attempt NIXL agent removal during peer teardown
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the stale NIXL peer-registration state in the P2P tiering transport that can permanently wedge the data plane after a peer-down/reconnect cycle such as SIGSTOP/SIGCONT, while the control plane keeps reporting HIT. Fixes #60205.

## Problem

`NixlTransport.remove_remote_peer()` runs two independent teardown operations in sequence: releasing the remote descriptor-list handle, then removing the remote agent. If `release_dlist_handle()` raises, the exception aborts the method before `remove_remote_agent()` is attempted, so the NIXL remote agent stays registered after the peer is gone — leaving a stale registration behind.

`_publish_peer()` has the same problem on its superseded-registration path: both teardown calls share a single `try` block, so a release failure skips the agent removal for a registration that is being discarded.

**Reporter's reproduction (#60205), condensed:** disaggregated prefill/decode, `TieringOffloadingSpec` over UCX/NIXL. After SIGSTOP of one EngineCore and SIGCONT, the control plane recovers (sessions reconnect, heartbeats and lookups keep returning HIT), but transfers to/from that rank fail permanently — `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`, then `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` on every poll. Fetches time out after 30 s and recompute; healthy ranks keep working; only a group restart fixes the wedged rank.

## Fix

Move both teardown calls into one small `_release_remote_handles()` helper that runs each operation under its own `try`/`except`, and call it from both `remove_remote_peer()` and `_publish_peer()`. Failures from either teardown operation are logged rather than aborting teardown midway, so `remove_remote_agent()` is always attempted. The `_peer_lock`/`_peer_gen` handling in `remove_remote_peer()` on `main` is unchanged.

## Evidence from the reviewer

The reviewer reproduced the stale-registration wedge on real NIXL/UCX: two pods on different nodes, nixl 1.5.0, `rc_mlx5` over InfiniBand, DRAM-only transfers, using the same call sequence as `NixlTransport`, with every WRITE checksum-verified at the target:

- Teardown plus a same-name re-add after a 249-second SIGSTOP/SIGCONT cycle recovers cleanly; the re-add does not reuse a stale endpoint.
- With the peer frozen, the WRITE raises `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT`. If `remove_remote_agent` was also skipped (the pre-patch path when `release_dlist_handle` raises), the SIGCONT plus re-add reports OK, but every WRITE after that still fails with `REMOTE_DISCONNECT` (3 attempts over ~2 min). This matches #60205.
- Calling `remove_remote_agent` unconditionally, then re-adding, recovers it.

## Important qualification

The regression tests simulate `release_dlist_handle()` raising. Why it raised in the original incident is not confirmed.

## Scope boundary

This PR does not claim to stop in-flight writes, change transfer polling semantics, or fix the server notification ordering — `remove_remote_peer()` does not stop an in-flight WRITE. Server notification ordering and transfer-terminal handling are covered by #59790; `poll()`/`NOT_FOUND` handling stays out of scope and will be decided jointly with #59790/#49632.

## Root cause and design

**Root cause.** `remove_remote_peer()` released the dlist before removing the remote agent with no error handling — if `release_dlist_handle()` raised, `remove_remote_agent()` never ran, orphaning the NIXL registration with no Python reference left. `_publish_peer()` shared one `try` block across both calls with the same skip-on-raise behavior.

**Why teardown failures are logged, not raised:** `remove_remote_peer()` runs inside `manager._reap_dead_sessions()`, which has no exception guard up to `get_finished_jobs()`; raising would abort the reap loop and propagate into the scheduler. The EC connector's NIXL transport follows the same log-and-continue pattern.

## Testing

Commands (run from the repo root):

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p        # 277 passed
python -m ruff check <changed files>                                                                      # passed
python -m ruff format --check <changed files>                                                             # passed
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD                                                                       # clean
```

New regression tests, both verified to fail against unpatched upstream `nixl.py` (negative control: 2 failed, exit 1) and pass with the fix:

- `test_remove_peer_removes_agent_even_if_release_fails` — a release failure during peer removal must not skip `remove_remote_agent()`.
- `test_superseded_registration_removes_agent_even_if_release_fails` — a release failure while discarding a superseded registration in `_publish_peer()` must not skip `remove_remote_agent()`.

Runs are CPU-only with a mocked NIXL agent, in WSL2 Ubuntu, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.1+cpu.

**Outstanding limitation:** no GPU/RDMA/UCX hardware validation was performed by the contributor. The hardware reproduction above was performed by the reviewer, not locally.

## Disclosure

This contribution was prepared with AI assistance (Codebuff).

## Overview

This PR adds an option to change the log level used for logging the request body JSON. 
This PR is related to the previously merged PR: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58163

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4] Remap Quark MTP layer_quant_config onto draft prefixes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp"}'` fails to load mixed Quark DeepSeek-V4 checkpoints (FP8 attention / shared experts + NVFP4 routed experts). The draft modules are constructed under `model.layers.{num_hidden_layers + i}.*`, but `_make_deepseek_v4_weights_mapper` rewrites Quark `layer_quant_config` keys from `mtp.{i}.*` to `model.mtp.{i}.*`. Per-layer lookups miss, every MTP linear falls back to the global NVFP4 scheme, and `PackedColumnParameter.load_merged_column_weight` then asserts on a packed vs unpacked shape mismatch.

This is independent of the ROCm PDL warmup fix in #56035.

## Changes

- Add `align_mtp_quant_config()` to re-key `model.mtp.{i}.` onto the draft prefixes before MTP construction.
- Give `DeepSeekV4MTP` the same `packed_modules_mapping` as `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` so fused `gate_up_proj` / `fused_wqa_wkv` unfold to `w1`/`w3` and `wq_a`/`wkv` for per-layer lookup.
- Apply on amd / nvidia / xpu MTP classes (same mapper mismatch exists on all three).

## Test plan

- [x] `vllm serve` DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 on 8× gfx950, TP=8, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`
- [x] MTP weights load (`MTP draft model loaded: 39 params`)
- [x] Greedy completion and a short chat request succeed
- [x] Speculative acceptance is non-zero (46/51 draft tokens accepted ≈ 90%)


## Test result

ROCm serve reached `Application startup complete`. `/health` 200. Greedy `"The capital of France is"` produced `" Paris."`; chat `"Name three prime numbers greater than 100"` produced `"101, 103, 107"`. Spec decode metrics: 51 draft tokens, 46 accepted.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Add PROMOTION_LATENCY histogram metric for tiering offload
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add the Prometheus histogram `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promotion_latency_seconds` for secondary-to-primary
promotion attempts, labeled by tier.
The histogram measures elapsed time from `TransferJob` creation until the tier reports completion. It includes time waiting in the tier queue and failed promotion attempts. It does not use `JobResult.transfer_time`, which measures
active data transfer only. P2P promotions are measured even when their `JobResult` has no `transfer_time`.


The `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promotion_latency_seconds` histogram has a `result` label with values `success` and `failure`.
- `success` is recorded when `JobResult.success` is `True`.
- `failure` is recorded when `JobResult.success` is `False`, including P2P load timeouts.
This keeps failed promotions visible while letting users query success and failure latency separately.


## Test Plan
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_metrics.py  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py -v
```
## Test Result
Add the actual command results after running the tests on the final branch.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Read VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS once per IterationStats
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`IterationStats.update_from_output` read `envs.VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` once per request output per step. This reads it once per `IterationStats` instead.

## Claims

- Removes one `envs` module `__getattr__` and two `os.getenv` calls per request output per step from the API-server output-processing loop. Measured on the installed vLLM (CPU, aarch64): `IterationStats.update_from_output` goes from 4.1 µs to 1.6 µs per output with the envs cache off, which is the API server's state today.
- No behaviour change: the flag is read at the start of each iteration instead of for each output within it.

## Validation

- py-spy GIL profile of a `vllm serve`-based worker streaming a few thousand concurrent requests: `update_from_output` → `envs.__getattr__` → the `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` lambda accounted for a little over 1% of all GIL-held samples in the API-server process. With the read hoisted that frame disappears.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py` passes.

## Details

`enable_envs_cache()` is only called in the multiprocess executor, so processes that run `OutputProcessor` (the API server, or any `AsyncLLM` host) always take the uncached path. The flag cannot change between outputs of one step in any meaningful way, so reading it per `IterationStats` keeps the semantics while taking it off the per-output path.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add AliceAI support
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Add native vLLM support for AliceAI.

[AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base](https://huggingface.co/yandex/AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base/blob/main/README_en.md)
is Yandex's Apache-2.0 base language model, trained from scratch. It has 80B
parameters, 3B active parameters per token, and a 262,144-token context.

Compared with Qwen3Next, AliceAI uses Kimi Delta Attention in place of Gated
DeltaNet, Block Attention Residuals in place of standard residual connections,
and sigmoid MoE routing with expert-score correction bias in place of softmax
routing.

The model has 36 KDA layers and 12 gated full-attention layers, 512 routed
experts with top-10 routing and one shared expert, and one MTP layer.

Our [published evaluations](https://huggingface.co/yandex/AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base/blob/main/README_en.md#benchmarks)
report 91.1 on MATH-500 and 86.5 on WikiWebFacts, a Russian factual-knowledge
benchmark, compared with 81.9 and 62.4 for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base. The model card
describes the evaluation setup and includes the full results.

This PR:

- adds standalone AliceAI model and MoE classes without modifying Qwen3Next
  or the model runner;
- loads AliceAIConfig from HF Hub; --trust-remote-code is required;
- reuses the existing Qwen3Next full-attention layer, Kimi KDA,
  Attention Residual primitive, and fused MoE implementation;
- implements the AliceAI decoder topology, sigmoid MoE routing with
  expert-score correction bias, and checkpoint weight mappings;
- ignores MTP weights and warns when the config declares MTP layers;
- registers the architecture and documents model support;
- adds focused tests to the existing CI test command.

No existing AliceAI implementation or competing open pull request was found.

- Pipeline parallelism is not supported; `pipeline_parallel_size=1` is required.
- LoRA adapters targeting Attention Residual projections are currently ignored.
- Sequence-parallel MoE is not supported.
- MTP speculative decoding is not supported in this PR.
- Speculative methods requiring auxiliary hidden states, including Eagle3, are
  not supported.
- CPU weight offloading is supported only with the UVA backend; the prefetch

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Register packed MLA KV rows as a single region
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With a block-outermost KV cache layout (`VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`), all layers' pages of a block sit in one contiguous row. 
NIXL still registers one region per layer, so each block moves as one descriptor per layer (effectively rendering BL* useless). 

This PR registers the row once, fixing registration back to its intended use.

Example: GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, BLHNC. Input to `register_kv_caches` on rank 0 is 99 views over one 43.8 GB storage:

```
model.layers.0.self_attn.indexer.k_cache  (14323, 1, 64, 132)  stride(0)=3059712  offset 0
model.layers.0.self_attn.attn             (14323, 1, 64, 576)  stride(0)=3059712  offset 177408
...

row b: [ idx L0 | idx L1 | ... | mla L0 | mla L1 | ... | mla L77 ]   3059712 B
```

**Before** (`elif storage_is_block_major:` branch), each view is its own region:

```
region 0:  base S + 177408, block_len 36864, stride 3059712   # layers.0.attn
region 1:  base S + 0,      block_len 8448,  stride 3059712   # layers.0.indexer
...
-> 99 regions, 99 x 14323 = 1.42M descriptors; a 2-block request = 198 descriptors
```

**After** (the existing whole-row branch, previously push-only), every view emits the same region and dedup folds them into one:

```
region 0:  base S, block_len 3059712, stride 3059712           # whole row, all layers
-> 1 region, 14323 descriptors; a 2-block request = 2 descriptors
```

### HiSparse

A HiSparse decoder can't register rows: its MLA cache is in host DRAM and its indexer on GPU, so it keeps per-layer regions LB*. 
P can still advertise each layer's `(offset, page_size)` within the row (BL*).
When the peer is per-layer, `_split_remote_packed_rows` (added with this PR) maps P's row onto the peer's per-layer regions.
 
BLHNC P + HiSparse D therefore works as before, with the same descriptor count as `main`.
cc @LucasWilkinson the alternative is to enforce P also uses LB* here, not sure if there's disadvantages (considering .

Out of scope: GQA spec-decode drafts under an MLA target, deferred to #60564.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py test_nixl_connector.py test_nixl_connector_hma.py test_nixl_push_connector.py`
  - `test_packed_mla_pp1_transfers_whole_rows` now covers pull and push and asserts 1 region / 1 descriptor per block, guarding against falling back to per-layer regions again.
  - New tests for the row split and for the mismatched-rows error.
- E2E, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, P TP4 -> D TP4 on 8xB200, NixlConnector pull, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 500` (5-shot) through `toy_proxy_server.py`.

## Test Result

- Unit: 593 passed across the four suites. On `main`, the new pull-mode cases of `test_packed_mla_pp1_transfers_whole_rows` fail (per-layer regions); with this PR they pass.

| P -> D | regions P / D | gsm8k | NIXL transfers | avg descriptors / transfer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLHNC -> BLHNC | 1 / 1 (99 / 99 on main) | 0.912 | 1040, 0 failed | 1.2 |
| BLHNC -> HiSparse D (default layout) | 1 / 99 | 0.918 | 685, 0 failed | 45.9 |

## Related PRs

#60851 and #60564 target the same descriptor blow-up. #60564 puts whole rows behind an opt-in `whole_row_regions` flag that must be set on both P and D, and rejects HiSparse. Here it is the default for BLHNC, needs no flag, and HiSparse decoders keep working. 

#60564 also handles GQA draft head-sharding, which this PR leaves to it.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Make finish_reason and Responses item status truthful
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53255, #58228, #57998. Also covers the `finish_reason` half of #53363 and #50889.

Chat `finish_reason` and Responses item `status` both claimed more than what happened:

- **Chat, non-streaming.** `tool_choice="required"` ending with engine `stop` but zero parsed tool calls returned `finish_reason="tool_calls"` next to an empty `tool_calls` array. An `auto` tool call parsed from a generation cut by `max_tokens` returned `tool_calls` instead of `length`, so a client could not tell a completed turn from one cut mid-arguments. The streaming path already guarded both (#46303), so the same request answered differently depending on `stream`. The `/derender` chat paths carried two more hand-written copies of the policy, one with the same `max_tokens` defect.
- **Responses, non-harmony.** Every `ResponseOutputMessage` and `ResponseFunctionToolCall` was hardcoded `status="completed"`, even inside a response whose top-level `status` is `incomplete` with `incomplete_details.reason = max_output_tokens`. The harmony path already did this correctly. In streaming the last `response.output_item.done` said `completed` and the stream ended with `response.completed` instead of the spec's `response.incomplete`.
- **Responses, harmony streaming.** The terminal-event code is shared, so a gpt-oss stream whose response status is `incomplete` now also ends with `response.incomplete` instead of `response.completed`.

### Relation to open PRs

This PR is a superset of the open partial fixes and makes all four sites share one rule:

- #53256 adds `and bool(tool_calls)` to the `required` clause only; leaves the `length` bug and both derender copies.
- #58286 gates the relabel on engine `stop` only; leaves the `required`-with-zero-calls bug, has conflicts.
- #47963 (streaming `length`) is superseded by the merged #46303.
- #47931 adds a fourth copy of the policy to derender; its e2e derender assertion is still useful on top of `resolve_finish_reason()`.
- #58018 fixes the non-harmony item status the same way (last item `incomplete`, streaming `close_current`); this PR covers that part and derives it from the same finish reason the chat rule uses. Its separate Harmony zero-delta lifecycle fix is independent and still stands.
- #45386 adds the `response.incomplete` terminal event; covered here (same `ResponseIncompleteEvent` wrapper and background-replay handling).

## Test Plan
Live A/B on H200 with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-model-len 4096` (plus a second pair of servers with no tool parser), this branch vs merge-base `dfc8e0f3e2`, 29 + 9 requests (chat non-stream/stream, `n=2`, Responses non-stream/stream, Anthropic) replayed twice at `temperature=0`. `max_tokens=18` cuts the model right after the closing brace of the tool-call JSON, so a call is parsed but the engine reports `length`.

## Test Result

Unit: 21 finish_reason tests and 130 Responses tests pass; full `test_serving_chat.py` 195 passed (GPT-OSS fixture errors also occur on main). `pre-commit` clean including mypy.

Live A/B, only these fields changed; every other response (complete calls, named, streaming chat, plain text, `n=2`, 400s without a parser) was byte-identical:

| Request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `tool_choice=auto`, `max_tokens=18` (call parsed, cut) | `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` | `"length"` |
| same, `stream=true` | `"length"` | `"length"` (now consistent) |
| `/v1/responses`, `max_output_tokens=6` (message cut) | item `status: "completed"` | `"incomplete"` |
| `/v1/responses`, `tool_choice=required`, `max_output_tokens=18` (call cut) | item `"completed"` | `"incomplete"` |
| same two, `stream=true` | `output_item.done: completed`, ends `response.completed` | `incomplete`, ends `response.incomplete` |
| no-parser server, `/v1/responses`, `max_output_tokens=6` | item `"completed"` | `"incomplete"` |
| `/v1/messages`, auto tool, `max_tokens=18` | `stop_reason: "tool_use"` | `"max_tokens"` |
| `required` / named with a complete call | `"tool_calls"` / `"stop"` | unchanged |

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 18,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What'"'"'s the weather in Paris? Use the tool."}],
  "tool_choice": "auto", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}]}'

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/responses -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "temperature": 0, "max_output_tokens": 6,
  "input": "Write a long paragraph about the sea.", "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}'
```

commits.pr_title: [Build][CPU] Install Run:ai Model Streamer in vllm-openai-cpu image
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add the `runai` wheel extra to the release-stage install in `docker/Dockerfile.cpu`, so the published `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu` image ships `runai-model-streamer` and can load the tokenizer with `--load-format runai_streamer`.

## Claims

- The CPU image is used as the CPU-side container of KV-cache-aware routers (llm-d-style EPP/inference-gateway deployments). No model weights are needed there — only the tokenizer and other non-tensor files, which are pulled from the object store through the Run:ai streamer path.
- Today this fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: runai_model_streamer` because the release stage installs only `dist/*.whl[audio,bench]` and `runai-model-streamer` is an optional dependency outside the wheel's install_requires. After this change, the tokenizer loading path works in the released CPU image.

## Validation

- `docker buildx build --check -f docker/Dockerfile.cpu .` — passes with 0 errors (only pre-existing `LegacyKeyValueFormat` warnings on unrelated `ENV` lines).
- Full image build + in-container check is pending and will be exercised by the CPU release image CI job (`.buildkite/image_build/image_build_cpu.sh`); recommended verification inside the built image:
  ```bash
  python -c "import importlib.util; print(importlib.util.find_spec('runai_model_streamer') is not None)"
  ```
- Platform compatibility is already exercised upstream: `requirements/test/cpu.txt` pins `runai-model-streamer==0.15.7`, so CPU CI already installs and tests the streamer against the CPU wheel; only the release image was missing it.

## Details

- The change reuses the existing `runai` extra from `setup.py` (`"runai": ["runai-model-streamer[s3,gcs,azure] >= 0.15.7"]`) instead of adding a new pin, so the version spec stays in one place and matches the CUDA `docker/Dockerfile` floor.
- The streamer itself is device-agnostic (tensors are streamed through CPU buffers); only the `distributed` streaming option requires CUDA/ROCm (see `docs/models/extensions/runai_model_streamer.md`).
- Not duplicating any existing PR: searched open PRs for "runai-model-streamer", "runai cpu dockerfile", and "Dockerfile.cpu" — no open PR adds the Run:ai streamer to the CPU image.
- Tradeoff: the image grows by the streamer and its S3/GCS/Azure SDK dependencies.
- AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Chore] Use upstream Transformers DeepseekV4Config
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Split from #60823: deletes the vendored `DeepseekV4Config` and ports the DeepSeek-V4 code to the upstream Transformers 5.16.1 schema. Also updates the `transformers-upgrade` skill.

Related PRs:
- **#60823:** the larger unvendoring PR this is split from; DeepSeek-V4 has been dropped from it.
- **#43443:** patches one reader of the popped `compress_ratios` (`attention.py`). This PR covers every reader, so it supersedes #43443.

## Claims

- Deletes `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/deepseek_v4.py`. Upstream folds `compress_ratios` and `num_hash_layers` into `layer_types` / `compress_rates` / `mlp_layer_types`:
  - V4-only code (attention, decoder, CPU/XPU/NVIDIA MoE, the C4/C128 CuTe DSL kernels) reads the upstream fields directly.
  - Code that also sees DeepSeek-V4.1 configs (the shared MLA backends, `mla_attention`, the arch convertor, the spec-decode proposer and the warmup kernels) uses `get_compress_ratios`. That helper returns V4.1's legacy field, or derives it from the upstream fields with the MTP layers appended. V4.1 can't move to the upstream schema: it uses compress ratios 1 and 2, which have no upstream layer type.
- `mm_prefix_span_leading_pad_modulus` moves from the config onto `DeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration`, where the model runner already looks for it. The sparse-SWA image-span widening is now keyed on an upstream `DeepseekV4Config` with `vision_n_layers > 0`, matching what the vendored config set.
- `is_rope_parameters_nested` accepts V4's `{"main", "compress"}` rope layout.
- No numerics change for DeepSeek-V4-Flash: greedy outputs are bit-identical to `main`, and GSM8k, GPQA Diamond and MTP acceptance match.
- **`transformers-upgrade` skill:**
  - Models in `vllm/models/` must run GSM8k and GPQA Diamond against `main`, and these evals should disable FlashInfer autotuning.
  - Adds two hazards: undeclared fields with no default, and top-level configs that no longer forward reads to `text_config`.
  - Adds a re-grep for old field names after rebasing.
  - Drops the PR and issue numbers from the skill.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on 8x B200, `main` (`bc3ddb198a`) on GPUs 0-3 vs this branch on GPUs 4-7, TP4 each, `transformers` 5.19.0.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8k, 5-shot, 1319 questions, autotune off | 0.944, 0.944 | 0.937, 0.947 |
| GSM8k with MTP (1 token), autotune off | 0.947 | 0.946 |
| MTP draft acceptance | 95.5% (57174 / 59896) | 95.4% (57041 / 59771) |
| GSM8k with MTP, rerun on 84f38ff455 | 0.948 | 0.949 |
| MTP draft acceptance, rerun on 84f38ff455 | 95.4% (57236 / 59977) | 95.5% (57494 / 60209) |
| GPQA Diamond, 8 repeats, reasoning effort high | 0.538 | 0.534 |
| Greedy decode, 4 short prompts x 64 tokens, autotune off | | bit-identical logprobs |

FlashInfer re-tunes its FP4 MoE tactics on every server start, even when given a cache. With autotuning on, the two servers picked different tactics and GSM8k drifted by about 1 point (0.947-0.951 vs 0.939-0.941). With `--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}'` greedy outputs match exactly, so the drift is tactic selection, not this change.

Config dumps for Flash, Flash-Vision-Exp and Pro, using the skill's scripts: `get_compress_ratios`, the per-layer upstream reads, the hash-layer count and the C4/C128 kernel flags all reproduce each checkpoint's legacy values exactly; the mm-prefix clamp is on only for Vision-Exp, as before; and the DeepSeek-V4 RoPE `cos_sin_cache` is bit-identical for sliding, CSA and HCA layers. Vision-Exp and Pro were not served (not enough disk on the host); Vision-Exp's `config.json` sets every `vision_*` field the processor reads.

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python tests/evals/gpt_oss/run_gpqa_eval.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --reasoning-effort high --base-url http://localhost:<port>/v1 --n-threads 128 --max-output-tokens 32768
```

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Advertise `--enable-x`/`--disable-x` for boolean CLI flags
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Boolean CLI flags named `enable_*` / `disable_*` now advertise `--enable-x` and `--disable-x` as each other's inverse, instead of argparse's `--no-enable-x` / `--no-disable-x`. The `--no-` spellings keep working but are hidden.

## Claims

- `--enable-x` and `--disable-x` are inverses for every `BooleanOptionalAction` flag whose name starts with `enable_` or `disable_` (50 on `vllm serve`):
  - `enable_prefix_caching`: `--enable-prefix-caching` sets it to `True`; `--disable-prefix-caching` sets it to `False`.
  - `disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager`: `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` sets it to `True`; `--enable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` sets it to `False`.
- **Backwards compatible:** `--no-enable-x` and `--no-disable-x` still parse, including from YAML configs (`enable_x: false`). They no longer appear in `--help`, the generated CLI docs or usage strings.
- **Other bool flags unchanged:** flags without the prefix (e.g. `--data-parallel-hybrid-lb`) keep `--x` / `--no-x`, and short aliases like `-ep` stay positive.
- **Docs and messages:** user-facing docs, examples and error messages now use the advertised spelling. Tests, CI and benchmark scripts keep `--no-enable-x`, which still works and exercises the compatibility path.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/utils_/test_argparse_utils.py tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py \
    tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_cli_args.py tests/benchmarks/test_rust_bench_cli_parity.py
```

213 passed (CPU only). The new tests in `test_argparse_utils.py` parse through a subcommand and an argument group and cover:

- both prefixes in both directions;
- a short alias (`-ef`);
- the underscore form (`--disable_feature`);
- the hidden `--no-` spellings;
- a plain `BooleanOptionalAction` that is unaffected;
- the usage string, which lists only the advertised options.

Every `vllm` subcommand parser still builds with no option-string conflicts: serve, launch render, preload, run-batch, and the bench subcommands throughput, latency, startup, mm-processor, serve and sweep.

`vllm serve --help=prefix-caching` now prints:

```
  --enable-prefix-caching, --disable-prefix-caching
  --enable-expert-parallel, -ep, --disable-expert-parallel
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager, --enable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
```

## Details

Follows the maintainer discussion on Slack. `--disable-x` reads more naturally than `--no-enable-x`, and flags that start with `disable_` should get `--enable-x` symmetrically. The original `BooleanOptionalAction` standardisation is kept; only the advertised names change.

**Implementation.** `FlexibleArgumentParser` registers `EnableDisableAction` in place of `BooleanOptionalAction` in its action registry. Argument groups and subparsers share that registry, so no call sites change. The action:

- registers the inverse prefix alongside argparse's `--no-` variants;
- decides the value from whether the option used was a negative one;
- has its `option_strings` trimmed back to the advertised ones after registration, so the `--no-` forms stay registered with the parser but leave help, usage and docs.

To trim after registration, the `add_argument` / argument-group overrides that previously existed only for Python < 3.13 (for the `deprecated` kwarg) are now unconditional; the `deprecated` handling inside them is still version-gated.

**Limitations.**

- If a parser defines both `--enable-x` (bool) and a separate `--disable-x` option, argparse raises a conflicting-option error at parser construction. No such pair exists today.
- `store_true` flags such as `--disable-log-stats` are untouched, since they have no inverse form today.

**Sequencing with #61489.** That PR points docs at `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`. Whichever of the two lands second should switch those references to `--disable-flashinfer-autotune`.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `disable alias enable flag argparse`, `no-enable disable cli alias` and `FlexibleArgumentParser disable`; nothing related.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject mismatched float16/bfloat16 KV cache dtype
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reject an explicit `float16`/`bfloat16` `kv_cache_dtype` that differs from the model dtype in `VllmConfig.__post_init__`, before backend selection and CUDA-graph capture. Fixes [#60859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60859).

No other open PR addresses this issue (`gh pr list --search "60859 in:body"`).

## Claims

- `dtype=bfloat16` with `kv_cache_dtype=float16` raises `ValueError` while the engine config is built, so `mha_varlen_fwd` never sees a bfloat16 query and a float16 key.
- The error is `kv_cache_dtype="float16" is incompatible with dtype="bfloat16". Please set --kv-cache-dtype to auto or bfloat16.`
- The swapped pair is rejected the same way. A `float32` model with an explicit `float16` KV cache is rejected with a hint to use `auto` only, because `float32` is not a legal `--kv-cache-dtype`.
- `"auto"`, a matching float16/bfloat16 pair, and FP8 stay valid.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k mismatched_float_kv_cache -q
```

6 passed: both mismatched float pairs and `float32` with a `float16` KV cache raise `ValueError`; matching `float16`, `"auto"`, and `"fp8"` are accepted. A direct `VllmConfig.__post_init__` call with a bfloat16 model and `kv_cache_dtype="float16"` raises the same error. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0) pass.

End-to-end `LLM.generate` on A6000 was not run (no CUDA GPU here).

## Details

**Root cause.** FlashAttention `mha_varlen_fwd` requires the query and the key to share a dtype. The engine accepted `dtype=bfloat16` and `kv_cache_dtype=float16`, then crashed during CUDA-graph capture.

**Why config-level.** The review asked to reject this mix once in `VllmConfig.__post_init__` rather than deselect backends. The check runs after `try_verify_and_update_config()`, so a model hook can still rewrite the cache dtype first (DeepSeek V3.2 rewrites an explicit `bfloat16` cache to `auto`). Triton can cast an unquantized KV tile up to the query dtype; this change refuses the mismatched pair instead of falling through to that path. The A100 data on #60859 supports rejecting rather than steering selection: FlashInfer asserts at init, and FlexAttention runs but produces silently wrong output (mean NLL 13.98 vs 3.96 with `auto`).

**AI assistance:** Used during diagnosis, implementation, and PR drafting. The human submitter reviewed the change and ran the checks above.
