commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't crash DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup when get_bf16_mega_gate_config is missing
commits.pr_body:
**Before:** A server started with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on a model whose MoE layers use the bf16 mega gate crashes during kernel warmup with `AttributeError: module 'deep_gemm' has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'`.

**After:** Warmup completes. When DeepGEMM does not export `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`, the MegaMoE warmup buckets M values by `block_m` only.

## Overview

#60468 made `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` call `dg.get_bf16_mega_gate_config` to pick one warmup M per gate config. #61149 moved the DeepGEMM pin to `6ce1c5ec`, which no longer exports that op. Every MegaMoE warmup that uses the mega gate now fails:

```
kernel_warmup.py:244 -> deep_gemm_warmup.py:511 -> :504 -> :366
AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'
```

This PR checks `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` and uses an empty gate config when the op is missing.

## Claims

- MegaMoE warmup no longer crashes when the installed DeepGEMM lacks `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`.
- Behavior is unchanged when the op is present.

## Validation

Existing unit tests:

```
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
# 8 passed
```

Real module, with the vendored DeepGEMM from the precompiled wheel (`vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`): `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` is `False`, and `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` (EP=4, 256 experts, top-k 6, 8192 tokens, mega gate on) now returns `[106, 256, 602, 2565, 7901, 8192]` instead of raising.

End to end on 4x B300: a DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192` finishes DeepGEMM warmup (1254/1254), passes `/health`, and answers a completion request ("The capital of France is" -> " Paris.").

No open PR fixes this: searching open PRs for `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` finds none, and #61538, which edits the same function, keeps the call.

## Details

Coverage trade-off: without gate configs, warmup no longer picks one M per distinct bf16 mega gate config. Gate configs that do not line up with a `block_m` bucket are not warmed and will JIT on the first request that hits them. This costs first-request latency, not correctness.

## Follow-up

A follow-up PR will reintroduce `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM and bump the vLLM pin, which restores full warmup coverage for the mega gate. This guard can stay afterwards so a mismatched external `deep_gemm` install does not crash the server.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix][MLA] Fix FP8 MLA prefill unpad for interleave-padded heads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
The gfx950 FP8 asm MLA prefill pads heads to a multiple of 16. When the target is a multiple of the real head count (8 → 16, e.g. Kimi-K2.x at TP8), `get_mla_padded_q` uses `repeat_interleave`, but the output was sliced back as `[:, :num_heads]`, which is only correct for tile padding. The model then attends with the wrong heads and produces garbage. Introduced by #51040.

## Claims
- Restores accuracy for interleave-padded head counts: Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4 TP8 GSM8K 0.027 → 0.933.
- No performance change: same kernels; the unpad copy is still one kernel at the same cost.
- Adds the 8-head (interleaved) case to `test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`.

## Validation
Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, fp8 KV cache. GSM8K 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions ... --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, num_concurrent=64:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Before (upstream main) | 0.0273 ± 0.0045 | 0.0235 ± 0.0042 |
| After (this PR) | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |

Torch profiler, random 1024/1024, 64 prompts, concurrency 64: 40 kernels per prefill MoE layer before and after.

Unit test on MI355X: `pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR | 12 passed |
| Upstream unpad, with the new test cases | 2 failed, 10 passed: only `test_fp8_prefill_matches_reference[128-8]` and `[512-8]` fail |

<details>
<summary>Failure details on the upstream unpad</summary>

- `[128-8]`: mismatched elements 81,670 / 131,072 (62.3%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- `[512-8]`: mismatched elements 230,240 / 524,288 (43.9%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- All tile-padded (12, 24) and unpadded (16) cases pass on both versions.
</details>

## Details
Real heads sit at stride `nhead // num_heads` after `repeat_interleave` and at `[0:num_heads]` after tiling; the fix selects accordingly. Existing test head counts (12, 16, 24) only exercised tile padding.
No duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this; #59966 changes `get_mla_padded_q` but keeps `repeat_interleave` for the divisor case.
AI assistance was used to prepare this change and description; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Nemotron-Parse] Do image rescale/normalize on the device
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Opts `NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration` into vLLM's existing `mm_device_do_normalize` path, so the fixed 2048x1664 canvas travels to the device as `uint8` and the rescale/normalize happens in `FusedMMInputNorm` instead of as single-threaded CPU work inside the engine process.

Please do aware this change depends on pending tied embedding fix for nemoparse2.0 embedding.

The checkpoint ships its image processor as remote code, and its `preprocess(self, images, return_tensors=None, **kwargs)` **ignores** the `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs that `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs` injects when the feature is on: it always runs `ToTensor` and normalizes from `self.do_normalize`. Setting the model flag alone would therefore normalize twice. The `_call_hf_processor` override replays the processor's own pipeline up to (but not including) `ToTensor` to produce the raw canvas, and raises -- pointing at `--no-mm-device-do-normalize` -- if a checkpoint does not expose that pipeline, so "feature on => `uint8`" holds by construction.

## Claims

- `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True`; `build_mm_input_norm()` builds the norm and `_process_image_input` applies it unconditionally, as in the other models that opt in. With the feature off that is `IdentityInputNorm`, i.e. a plain cast.
- With the feature off, behaviour is identical to today.
- Both published checkpoints are handled: v1.2 (albumentations `transform` branch) and 2.0 (`_pad_to_size` branch).
- Payload per request drops 40.89 MB fp32 -> 10.22 MB uint8.

## Validation

Run on the latest `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` = `0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3`, whose `nemotron_parse.py` is byte-identical to this patch's parent and whose `layers/fusion/mm_input_norm.py` is byte-identical to this branch -- so the Triton `forward_cuda`, `IdentityInputNorm` and `_load_norm_params` exercised here are the ones this change targets. One H100, `--dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 --max-num-seqs 16`.

Greedy request on a sample document page (`max_tokens 512, temperature 0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, skip_special_tokens false`):

| engine | flag | dtype at model | `input_norm` | output sha256[:16] | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| patched | on | `uint8` | `FusedMMInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| patched | off | `bfloat16` | `IdentityInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | off | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | on | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |

Unpatched + on logs `Model does not support mm_device_do_normalize, forcing ... False`, confirming the flag is the only opt-in.

**Numerics** -- device path vs the host path it replaces:

| case | bf16 | fp16 | fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| real page, 10,223,616 elements | **equal, 0 mismatched** | equal, 0 | max abs 2.4e-07 |
| all 3x256 possible byte values | **equal, 0 mismatched** | 3 at 1 ULP | max abs 4.8e-07 |
| `forward_cuda` vs `forward_native` | equal, 0 | equal, 0 | max abs 1.2e-07 |



**Latency**, 3 interleaved reps per arm, fresh server each, identical flags:

| | encoder-only p50 (`max_tokens=1`) | c=1 p50 | c=8 aggregate |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | **132.5 ms** | **131.8 ms** | 937.9 tok/s |
| off | 263.1 ms | 261.5 ms | 772.7 tok/s |

**1.99x**, with the per-rep ranges non-overlapping across all six reps, and +21% aggregate throughput at c=8. 

The win is, An isolated single-threaded CPU microbenchmark attributes the win: the processor's float work goes 160.3 ms -> 5.9 ms.

The added `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron_parse.py` passes (2 passed).

Re-verified after making `input_norm` unconditional, same nightly, one H100: both flag arms produce identical output (`b37da04a78014080`, 5 greedy reps each), TTFT p50 226.8 -> 118.6 ms. With the feature off the unconditional call is bit-identical to the `pixel_values.to(dtype)` it replaces -- 0 differing elements of 10,223,616, in bf16, fp16 and fp32 -- so the default path is unchanged. Deleting `_resize_with_aspect_ratio` or `_pad_to_size` from the processor raises a `RuntimeError` naming `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`.

## Details

`_build_uint8_canvas` depends on three attributes of the checkpoint's remote-code image processor: `_resize_with_aspect_ratio`, `_pad_to_size` and `transform`. Two are private by convention and none is a stable API. If they change, the lookup raises and the error names `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`, so the failure is loud instead of a silent loss of the speedup. The cleaner fix lives in the checkpoint: `preprocess` should honour its own `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs, after which this override can be deleted entirely. I am happy to drop the override and gate the feature on that instead if reviewers prefer.

Reproducing the `b37da04a78014080` output on `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` additionally requires the tied-`lm_head` fix (#60272, a re-land of #53020); without it that checkpoint's output head is randomly initialized and the server emits garbage while reporting healthy. That fix is independent of this change and was applied only for the validation runs above.

Not covered: CUDA only (`forward_xpu` / `forward_oot` are untouched and untested); one image per request, which is this model's `get_supported_mm_limits`.

- `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/moe/parallel_utils.py` — passed all applicable hooks.
- Exact B200 FusedMoE retry in Buildkite #88300 — 20 passed (unpatched baseline/reproduction evidence).

No model evaluation is needed because this changes only test-process rendezvous.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CI] Fix renderers tests broken by tool name removal from warn logs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

[#59294](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59294) removed the tool name from the two malformed-`arguments` warnings in `vllm/renderers/chat_utils/chat_message.py`, but did not update `tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py`, which still asserts the name appears in the emitted record. Seven tests have failed on `main` since it merged.

That PR's own `:computer: (CPU) Reasoning + Renderers` job failed for this reason ([build 94769](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94769)) and it was merged red, so the breakage landed on `main` and now fails for every PR that touches a `cpu-async-engine-deps` path.

## Fix

Drop the four tool-name assertions and keep each test asserting the part of the message that still exists. The tool name was the only thing distinguishing `test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_large` from the small-payload case, so it asserts on the logged length instead, which is what actually covers the point of having a large case: an 18 KB payload is summarised by length rather than logged.

The source change in #59294 is left alone: not logging the tool name is the intended behavior.

## Validation

```
$ pytest -q tests/renderers/test_chat_utils.py -k tool_call_arguments
12 passed
```

Failing tests before this change, all with the same shape:

```
FAILED renderers/test_chat_utils.py::test_tool_call_arguments_malformed_json_small
  assert 'exec' in 'Tool call has arguments that are not valid JSON (54 chars);
  coercing to an empty object so the conversation can continue.'
```

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward: exact-shape forward timing
commits.pr_body:
> Commits: *[Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward*, the *model-microbenchmark* agent skill, and *Support DCP*. No changes to the model runner or model code.

## Overview

Add `vllm bench forward`: time the model forward of an **exact** batch (prefill, chunked prefill, prefix hit, decode, spec-decode verify, or any mix), built without the scheduler and run through the real `execute_model`, captured as a one-shot CUDA graph. Works single-GPU and with DP/TP/EP/DCP across nodes via `torchrun`.

```bash
vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --case decode=64*1@8192 --case prefill=8192 --case mix=4096,32*1@8192
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model ... -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --shapes shapes.json
```

## Claims

- Exact shapes: requests are `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` (query length, KV length including the query, draft tokens). A prefill's prefix is a prefix-cache hit (SWA bounded replay on DeepSeek-V4.1) unless `c` marks a chunked prefill. Every run checks that the runner built exactly that batch.
- Accurate GPU time: one-shot FULL graph even for prefill (host-side plans are correct by construction, since the graph only replays the batch it captured). Rendezvous and timing events live inside the graph, so rank skew and launch gaps are excluded; each replay is reduced with MAX over ranks; per-replay jitter is reported (sample spread) and flagged above 0.5%.
- Realistic defaults for dummy weights: KV lengths vary +-50% (same on every DP rank, `--kv-len-jitter`); MoE routing is balanced per EP rank (`--routing auto`), replacing the degenerate routing of dummy gates.
- Matches independent references (below).

## Validation

GB200. CLI and unit tests (Benchmarks CLI job runs `tests/benchmarks/`):

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 3 passed
```

Against serving (decode, same model/config, `vllm bench latency` per-step time from 65- vs 1-token runs, FULL decode graph):

| Model | bench forward | serving step | gap (sampler, LM head, step overhead) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-0.6B, 32 x 4K context | 3.48 ms | 3.69 ms | 0.21 ms |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (43 layers, 1 GPU), 32 x 4K | 7.94 ms | 8.93 ms | 0.99 ms |

Against a standalone DeepSeek-V4.1 forward harness (recorded Sept 16; same shapes and config: DEP4, MegaMoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV; ~100K KV, decode):

| batch | harness | bench forward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 6.39 ms | 6.31 ms |
| 8 | 9.97 ms | 9.85 ms |
| 32 | 15.77 ms | 15.58 ms |
| 128 | 20.07 ms | 19.97 ms |

DCP: Kimi-K3 (9 layers, MLA) TP4 with DCP1 vs DCP4 on decode, chunked prefill and prefix hit: the runner builds the expected batches, DCP4 allocates the scheduler's block count (`block_size * dcp` tokens per block for DCP-sharded specs), and replays are deterministic.

Also run: DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DEP4 (1 node) and DEP8 (2 nodes, MNNVL), TEP4, prefix hits, verify. Median run-to-run reproducibility within ~0.3%; sample spread mostly 0.01-0.4% (higher on V4.1 DEP prefill, from MegaMoE cross-rank sync and host engram reads).

## Details

- **Flow per case:** build `SchedulerOutput` (disjoint block IDs across KV groups) -> zero the case's KV blocks -> `execute_model` twice: eager warmup (JIT, autotune), then capture/validate/time. For those two steps the bench shadows `runner.prepare_inputs` (to check the batch the runner built) and `model.forward` (to take over the eager model call) with instance attributes, then deletes them; the runner itself is unchanged. Requests are re-added on the second call; `sample_tokens` is never called, so the pending step state is dropped.
- **State restore:** the KV blocks a step writes are snapshotted and restored inside the graph before each replay, so in-place state (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1's compressor) is identical across replays.
- **KV init:** zeros only for now (`--kv-init zeros`). Random KV was measured within 3% on DeepSeek-V4.1 at ~100K context, so its per-layout model code isn't worth it yet.
- **Routing:** forward hooks on `GateLinear` replace gate logits with a balanced fixture; this covers backends that route from logits, including monolithic FlashInfer TRTLLM (verified on Kimi-K3) and modular (verified on DeepSeek-V4: router top-k equals the fixture). Models that compute top-k themselves (e.g. MegaMoE's fused gate on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and Kimi-K3) instead get the fixture's `topk_ids` through a forward pre-hook on any experts module whose `forward` takes `topk_ids`; on DeepSeek-V4.1 DEP4 this matches the earlier model-local override within run-to-run noise (+0.05% to +0.8%). Grouped top-k is rejected; layers the fixture can't reach fail loudly.
- **Model code:** none.
- **Dependencies / limitations:**
  - Dummy-loaded DeepSeek-V4.1 loses MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (fixed by #60096); the bench's dummy loader finalizes early as a temporary workaround (TODO to remove).
  - Data-dependent kernels need realistic activations: #61323 keeps dummy norms neutral (e.g. V4.1 sparse top-k 27.8 ms -> 10.7 ms, real weights 10.6 ms).
  - The batch builder mirrors scheduler semantics (block counts, prefix-hit replay); the unit test and the per-run layout check guard against drift.
  - Model branches on `is_current_stream_capturing()` (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 short-context top-k, V4.1 mHC overlap) make small batches' graph output differ slightly from eager; reported, not asserted.
- **Agent skill:** `.agents/skills/model-microbenchmark` documents usage and pitfalls (dummy-weight artifacts, torch.compile models, timing spread) for agents.
- **Size:** ~1,050 non-test lines, isolated under `vllm/benchmarks/forward/` plus the CLI entry, docs and agent skill.

commits.pr_title: [Model Runner V2] Enable batch-sharded sampling for GPT-OSS
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #61256.

Enable batch-sharded sampling for GPT-OSS by implementing
`GptOssForCausalLM.compute_logits_local`.

Without this hook, the V2 runner falls back to regular sampling even when
batch-sharded sampling is enabled.

## Claims

- Reuse the existing logits processor with `skip_gather=True` to return
  rank-local vocabulary logits.
- Preserve the default sampling path when sharding is disabled.
- Extend coverage to GPT-OSS and retain Llama coverage, including a
  single-request case that leaves one TP rank with no sampling requests.

## Validation

### Correctness and regression tests

Local validation used two NVIDIA L20 GPUs with TP=2, Python 3.12.14,
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, and source base
`61f084b5f3e58aa3d3ebc86aeaf4686c460c478`.

GPT-OSS tests use the organization-hosted checkpoint
`trl-internal-testing/tiny-GptOssForCausalLM`, with both model and tokenizer
pinned to `e82685101216af1953707faa42567d232a5e4d45`.

- `test_sharded_sampling.py`: **12 passed**, including all three GPU cases:
  `llama`, `llama-empty-rank`, and `gpt-oss`.
- GPT-OSS stability check: **10/10 independent-process runs passed**,
  with no skips or retries.
- Shared sharder and dry-sampler regression tests: **18 passed**.

The E2E cases compare generated tokens and log probabilities between
regular and sharded sampling. When sharding is enabled, the generic
helper also checks rank-local vocabulary width and exact equivalence
between gathered local logits and full logits.

Negative tests confirmed that:
- Removing the GPT-OSS hook fails the sharding-enabled assertion.
- Returning full logits from either the GPT-OSS or Llama hook fails the
  shard-width assertion.

Local Llama validation used the ModelScope mirror
`LLM-Research/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct@master`. The committed test retains
`meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`.

Relevant checks were run individually and passed. The full pre-commit
invocation was terminated during hook-environment installation, so a
complete pre-commit pass is still pending. Upstream GPU CI remains pending.

### Performance

Previously measured with GPT-OSS-20B on 2× L20, TP=2, concurrency 256,
256 input tokens and 128 output tokens. Each configuration used three
independent server runs, with 8 warm-up and 512 measured requests per run.

| Sampling | Baseline output tok/s | Sharded output tok/s | Throughput change | Mean TPOT change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| temperature=1, top_p=1 | 4385.4 | 4582.2 | +4.49% | -6.05% |
| temperature=1, top_p=0.95 | 4277.9 | 4533.4 | +5.97% | -7.13% |

These measurements used compilation/CUDA graphs and the default
FlashInfer sampler, with prefix caching disabled. The environment used
source base `61f084b5f` with native extensions from the official cu129
wheel for its parent commit `2eb491e18`.

The review changes affect tests only; these benchmarks were not rerun.
No Llama serving-performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

The production change only adds the GPT-OSS local-logits hook.

The direct logits helper is model-agnostic and runs for every
sharding-enabled test case. Its shard-width assertion catches an
incorrect full-logits implementation that token comparisons alone
may miss.

As discussed in review, shared LoRA compatibility validation is tracked
separately in #56074 as a follow-up.

Assisted by Astra.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Support Decision 3.0 decision models (vllm-sr/d3)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Serve the Decision 3.0 decision models ([`vllm-sr/d3`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3) and its smaller variants such as `vllm-sr/d3-mini` and `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) from their Hub checkpoints as they are: `vllm serve vllm-sr/d3`, then ask typed questions on `/v1/systemone`. Today these checkpoints do not load in vLLM (`Qwen3_5Model` is not a registered architecture and the readout is a separate file). This builds on vLLM's Qwen3.5 implementation, the structured decisions API (#60465 and its predecessors) and the Clef-Flash detection pattern (#61308).

## Claims

- **The published checkpoints load unchanged** (measured here: d3, d3-mini and d3-edge; see Follow-ups). A bare `Qwen3_5Model` checkpoint that ships a `decision_config.json` is detected and served as `D3ForSequenceClassification`. The 255-row answer-code readout (`readout.safetensors`) becomes the FP32 `score` head. The declared `noncausal_full_attention` makes the full attention layers bidirectional, while the Gated DeltaNet layers stay causal. Tied embeddings need nothing, and per-model `layer_types` are honoured (d3-edge: `llFllFllFFFF`).
- **`/v1/systemone` gives the checkpoint runtime's answers.** For each question, `D3Strategy` writes the prompt the checkpoint's own `d3_format.py` writes (byte-identical on 416 prompts), reads the question's codes from the classify head, and applies the option mask and the checkpoint temperature. It supports choice (up to 255 options), yes / no and score questions, text and JSON states, and images and videos read with the runtime's budgets (1.6 MP images; 2 fps, at most 32 frames of 0.2 MP).
- **Same decisions as the reference runtime on AMD Instinct MI325X.** Against `AutoModel.from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)`: 0 of 416 decisions changed on d3, 1 on d3-mini and 2 on d3-edge, all ties or near-ties. The median probability difference is 0.0024 to 0.0029.
- **Throughput.** On a mixed text / JSON / image / video load at 8 and 64 closed-loop clients, vLLM sustains 1.4x to 2.6x the rate of the checkpoint's own server (AutoModel behind HTTP, one request at a time).

## Validation

Hardware and software: one AMD Instinct MI325X per side. vLLM used the official ROCm nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-5555a2d8f7116b2b4877f66516f4128176cf722a` (PyTorch 2.13, ROCm 7.2), with this branch's Python tree (main `f4b8d43a6` plus this PR) overlaid; no kernels were built. The reference used the same image with the versions the checkpoint pins (transformers 5.17.0, flash-linear-attention 0.5.2). vLLM ran with no flags: `vllm serve vllm-sr/<model>`. Models: `vllm-sr/d3` @ fc2d74bd, `vllm-sr/d3-mini` @ 6d8971f4, `vllm-sr/d3-edge` @ fe71f8e1.

**Answers vs the reference** (`model.system_one(...)` in process): 416 questions per model, namely 3 states (a support ticket, release notes, a JSON account) x 128 typed questions (48 choice, 40 yes / no, 40 score), plus 1-, 4- and 16-question text, a 4-question JSON state, a 40-option choice, an image with 1 and 4 questions, and a 10 s 1080p video. The decision is the top choice, `noul >= 0.5`, or a score's most likely level; |dp| is the largest absolute probability difference over a question's options.

| Model | Decisions changed | Median abs dp | p90 | Max | Image / video questions, max abs dp |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| d3 (27B) | 0 / 416 | 0.0024 | 0.0078 | 0.027 | 0.0049 / 0.021 |
| d3-mini (4B) | 1 / 416 (0.5003 vs 0.4996) | 0.0026 | 0.0078 | 0.032 | 0.018 / 0.032 |
| d3-edge (0.6B) | 2 / 416 (margins 0.0019, 0.0012) | 0.0029 | 0.012 | 0.043 | 0.0050 / 0.0055 |

For scale, two vLLM configurations of d3 (defaults vs `--max-model-len 32768`, so different batch shapes) differ from each other by up to 0.011 and change 2 decisions.

**Throughput and latency**: closed loop, 30 s per level after an 8 s warm-up, over a mix of 40 % one-question text, 20 % four-question text, 10 % four-question JSON state, 10 % 40-option choice, 15 % new 1.6 MP image and 5 % new 10 s 1080p video. Every image and video carries new bytes. Each cell gives req/s and p50 / p90 latency in ms:

| Model | Side | 1 client | 8 clients | 64 clients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | checkpoint server | 6.9 (69 / 290) | 6.1 (1,210 / 1,653) | 4.6 (9,300 / 9,817) |
| d3 | vLLM | 6.7 (74 / 265) | 8.6 (903 / 1,228) | 8.5 (5,907 / 6,552) |
| d3-mini | checkpoint server | 17.0 (23 / 123) | 23.3 (339 / 499) | 18.3 (3,157 / 3,427) |
| d3-mini | vLLM | 15.8 (30 / 103) | 43.0 (166 / 273) | 45.0 (1,357 / 1,606) |
| d3-edge | checkpoint server | 31.6 (7.4 / 66) | 47.3 (141 / 306) | 41.7 (1,463 / 1,724) |
| d3-edge | vLLM | 28.6 (10 / 56) | 102 (23 / 211) | 110 (36 / 2,679) |

One request at a time (p50 ms, AutoModel in process / vLLM):

| Model | 1 text question | 16 text questions | new image, 1 question | new image, 4 questions | new 10 s video |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | 55.9 / 54.9 | 583 / 547 | 293 / 216 | 1,020 / 700 | 519 / 443 |
| d3-mini | 18.1 / 19.4 | 114 / 116 | 111 / 64 | 341 / 158 | 319 / 261 |
| d3-edge | 6.4 / 7.0 | 21.2 / 29.0 | 56 / 33 | 140 / 48 | 266 / 234 |

**Start-up and memory** (launch to the first answer; cold = empty compile caches, model files on local disk):

| Model | AutoModel cold / warm | vLLM cold / warm | GPU memory above idle, steady: AutoModel / vLLM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d3 | 39.9 / 22.0 s | 214.5 / 130.0 s (`--max-model-len 32768`: 139.0 / 67.8 s, same throughput) | 52 / 199 GiB |
| d3-mini | 28.6 / 10.5 s | 136.2 / 61.7 s | 11 / 216 GiB |
| d3-edge | 27.0 / 8.2 s | 129.2 / 37.1 s | 3.5 / 227 GiB |

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/models/multimodal/pooling/test_d3.py`: d3-edge vs the checkpoint runtime, with text prompts as token ids (including a 40-option choice) and one image prompt processed by vLLM. PASSED on MI325X (134 s).
- `pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k "decision_config or joint_head"`: 8 passed.
- `pytest tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/`: 115 passed, including the new d3 strategy tests.
- `pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k D3`: 2 passed.
- `pre-commit run` on the diff: all hooks pass. actionlint was skipped locally because no workflow files changed.

## Details

- **Detection** follows Clef-Flash: `Qwen3_5ModelArchConfigConvertor` maps `architectures: ["Qwen3_5Model"]` plus `decision_config.json` to `D3ForSequenceClassification` and keeps the decision config on `hf_config`. Bare `Qwen3_5Model` checkpoints without that file are unaffected (they stay unsupported, as today).
- **Config hook** `D3ForSequenceClassificationConfig` validates `format_version` 1, `pooling: last` and the attention mode. It sets `is_causal=False` for `noncausal_full_attention`, so chunked prefill and prefix caching turn off by themselves, sets `id2label` to the 255 codes, and makes the classify head return raw code logits by default. Probabilities only exist over a question's own options, so `/classify` and `/pooling` callers mask and normalize themselves.
- **Model** (`d3.py`): `as_seq_cls_model(Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration)`, so no LM head is allocated and the `score` head is FP32. It adds a mapper for the bare-backbone keys, `readout.safetensors` as `score.weight` via `secondary_weights`, and a processing info that applies the runtime's media budgets. The checkpoint's processor config allows 16.7 MP images, while the runtime reads at most 1.6 MP; video frames use transformers' `cap_pixels_per_frame` with the runtime's 200,704-pixel cap.
- **Strategy**: one classify read per question. The media come first, so they are processed once per request and shared by its questions, and the encoder cache deduplicates the vision tower. Videos go through the existing `qwen3_vl` loader, whose sampling rule already matches the runtime's, with `max_frames=32`. A small change to the question builder, `DecisionLimits.labeled`, lets label-free strategies accept more options than the A to Z label set; the defaults of other strategies are unchanged.
- **Why not an example client**: the System One API already has question types on main, so the option mask and temperature belong in the strategy rather than in client code.
- **Tradeoffs and limits**
  - Start-up: with chunked prefill off, the profiling pass runs one `max_model_len`-token sequence. At the config's 262,144 tokens this dominates start-up (71 s of d3's 130 s warm start). `--max-model-len 32768` halves it, with no throughput change on this mix.
  - Memory: vLLM reserves `--gpu-memory-utilization` (0.92) of HBM. The Gated DeltaNet layers still keep per-request state, and the attention layers keep no KV.
  - Media under load: at 64 clients, text stays fast (d3-edge text p90 about 80 ms) while image and video requests queue (image p50 2.65 s), because decoding a new 300-frame 1080p video per request is CPU-bound. `--renderer-num-workers 4` did not change this.
  - Small-model latency: one request at a time, multi-question requests on the small models are slower than in process (d3-edge, 16 questions: 29.0 vs 21.2 ms), since each question is its own engine request.
  - API differences from the runtime: a request with an invalid or too-long question returns 400 instead of per-question errors; at most 64 questions per request (the API's limit); `confidence` and `usage` follow `/v1/systemone`'s definitions; option descriptions, instructions and score levels are rendered as text (non-string values go through `str`, where the runtime writes JSON); the runtime's optional `permutation_average` is not available.
  - Not measured: d3-flash, d3-nano and d3-lite (same layout and code path), CUDA GPUs, tensor parallelism, LoRA.
- **Not a duplicate**: no open or closed PR or issue covers these checkpoints, `decision_config.json` readout checkpoints, or bare `Qwen3_5Model` loading (searched for d3, Decision 3.0, `Qwen3_5Model`, `decision_config.json`, decider, readout). The Laya PR (#58429) adds an unrelated ModernBERT-based model.
- **AI assistance** was used for the code, tests, measurements and this description. The PR stays a draft until the submitter has reviewed every line.

## Follow-ups

- **The other five Decision 3.0 models** (`vllm-sr/d3-flash`, `vllm-sr/d3-mini`, `vllm-sr/d3-nano`, `vllm-sr/d3-lite`, `vllm-sr/d3-edge`) share d3's architecture and take the same code path: each Hub checkpoint is a bare `Qwen3_5Model` with a `d3-code-readout-v1` `decision_config.json` (`noncausal_full_attention`, 255 codes) and a `readout.safetensors`. The variations between them, tied embeddings and d3-edge's layer layout, are exercised by d3-mini and d3-edge.
- **d3-mini and d3-edge** already match the reference in this PR's measurements (1 and 2 of 416 decisions changed, all ties or near-ties; see the agreement and throughput tables under Validation).
- **A follow-up PR** will validate d3-flash, d3-nano and d3-lite, publish agreement and throughput for all five, and add them explicitly to the docs examples and tests where it makes sense.

## Overview

The optional `(DGX) Spark FlashInfer NVFP4 XQA` step fails before reaching the kernel: the Spark agent cannot read the gated `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B`, which `create_vllm_config()` uses by default. This switches the test to `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, which the same file already uses.

- `test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness` no longer fails with `OSError: You are trying to access a gated repo` on agents without access to the meta-llama repo.
- The test only uses the model to build its config. Q/K/V are random tensors, the reference is the fa2 prefill over the same tensors, and the head layout is overridden, so the values the test uses do not change.

## Validation

All four parametrizations failed with the gated-repo error in both CI builds of #60948 that ran this optional step (`ready-run-all-tests`). Locally, with an empty HF cache and no token, `create_vllm_config()` reproduces the same `OSError` for `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B` and builds the config for `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.

After the test's overrides, both models give the same dtype (bf16), 24 query / 4 KV heads, head size 256, no sliding window or softcap, block size 16 and `nvfp4` cache dtype; only the architecture name differs.

The kernel part of the test has not run on SM12x yet, in CI or locally.

The step was added in #60452 as optional, so it stays blocked unless someone unblocks it or the PR has `ready-run-all-tests`; it had not run before #60948. Other tests in this file keep the default model because they run on agents that can read the gated repo.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Make the query contiguous for TRTLLM ragged MLA prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`TRTLLM_RAGGED` MLA prefill passes the query straight to FlashInfer's `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek`, whose launcher forwards K/V strides but not Q strides, so a strided query is read as if it were packed and prefill attention is silently wrong. This makes the query contiguous at both call sites (a no-op for callers that already pass a contiguous query, such as native models).

The Transformers modeling backend hits this because it hands MLA a transposed query (`[1, heads, tokens, dim] -> [tokens, heads, dim]`), and `TRTLLM_RAGGED` is the default MLA prefill backend on Blackwell.

## Claims

- Fixes MLA prefill for strided queries with `TRTLLM_RAGGED`, which broke every MLA model on the Transformers backend on Blackwell (e.g. GLM-4.7-Flash gsm8k 0.8% -> 83.5%, native 83.6%).
- No change for contiguous queries.

## Validation

GLM-4.7-Flash, gsm8k (5-shot, 1319 questions), 1x B200:

| Config | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| Native | 83.6% | 0.1% |
| Transformers backend, `main` | 0.8% | 31.8% |
| Transformers backend, this PR | 83.5% | 0.0% |

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --max-model-len 8192 [--model-impl transformers]
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000
```

On a small random-weight GLM-4.7-Flash-architecture checkpoint, the first generated token's logprob vs HF eager (same prompt, teacher-forced) went from 0.19 off to 0.00 with `TRTLLM_RAGGED`. Other MLA backends were already correct with the strided query: `FLASH_ATTN` prefill, and `FLASHINFER_MLA` / `CUTLASS_MLA` / `TRITON_MLA` decode.

Tests on B200:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_registry.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_selector.py  # 47 passed
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k TRTLLM_RAGGED  # 580 passed
```

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Drop two dead per-step ops from the AITER sparse MLA metadata build
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs once per KV-cache group per scheduler step and launches two GPU ops whose results are not needed:

1. **Unused `query_lens`.** `build()` computes `query_start_loc[1:] - query_start_loc[:-1]`, but `generate_sparse_seqlen_triton` only reads its size and device; the kernel derives per-request lengths from `cu_query_lens`. The parameter is dropped and `num_seqs` is taken as `cu_query_lens.size(0) - 1`.
2. **Self-aliasing `fill_`.** `paged_kv_indptr[n + 1:].fill_(paged_kv_indptr[n])` passes a view of the tensor being filled, so ATen clones the value first. A broadcast `copy_` from the same element writes the same values without the clone.

| op | aten ops | GPU kernels |
|---|---|---|
| `x[n+1:].fill_(x[n])` | `fill_` → `clone` (`empty_strided` + copy) → `copy_` | 2 |
| `t.copy_(x[n].expand_as(t))` | `copy_` | 1 |
| `qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]` | `sub` (+ alloc) | 1 |

Each `build()` launches two fewer kernels and makes two fewer device allocations, with no change in output. #57885 removed a similar dead op from the DSA indexer builder.

On ROCm, sparse-MLA layers that do not bring their own backend select `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`. Of 18 current checkpoints probed on main (dummy weights, 8 layers, TP=1), three reach this `build()`:

| model | binding | `build()` per decode step |
|---|---|---:|
| GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`) | `DeepseekV32MLAAttention` → `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` | 2 |
| GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 (`glm_moe_dsa`) | same | 2 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, DSA every 4th layer) | `MLAAttention` → `ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend` | 1 |

DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro and V4.1-Flash use their own builders, and the other 12 have no sparse MLA. CUDA never selects this backend.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py`. The new `test_build_fills_paged_kv_indptr_tail` poisons the `paged_kv_indptr` tail and checks that it reads as the running total; it fails if the tail copy is removed.
- Output equivalence: every benchmark run hashes the full `paged_kv_indptr` buffer (tail poisoned first), the returned metadata tensors and the AITER work/reduce metadata.
- Micro: the real `build()` on a builder constructed from a real `VllmConfig` (`max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, top-k 2048, decode B ∈ {1, 7, 29, 61, 127}). Both implementations alternate on one builder, order flipped every pair, 300 warmup + 3000 pairs, in 3 processes. *Steady*: contexts > top-k, so the persistent-metadata key hits. *Growing*: the key misses, so `get_mla_metadata_v1` and a stream sync run on every build.
- e2e: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (fp8 KV faults on main with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, before and independent of this PR), a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm with the first discarded.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1031 --random-output-len 509 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 509 --max-concurrency 61 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```
- e2e: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype auto` (fp8 KV faults on main with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, before and independent of this PR), a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm with the first discarded.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1031 --random-output-len 509 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 509 --max-concurrency 61 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```
- Accuracy: `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=2, `max_model_len=4096`, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `seed=1234`.

## Test Result

**Unit:** 5 passed on MI355X (gfx950), main `863475eb9c`. Output hashes match between the arms for every config and batch size.

**Micro**, MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.12.0, main `c961121519`:

| config | B | main (µs) | PR (µs) | paired Δ per call (µs), median [min, max] of 3 processes | gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| GLM-5.3, steady (AITER persistent path) | 1 | 91.48 | 80.68 | 10.82 [9.71, 10.89] | +11.2 % |
| | 29 | 91.29 | 81.22 | 10.12 [9.71, 10.66] | +11.0 % |
| | 127 | 91.62 | 81.22 | 10.55 [10.00, 10.59] | +11.1 % |
| GLM-5.3, growing (metadata recompute every build) | 1 | 162.81 | 149.77 | 12.81 [11.92, 13.91] | +8.3 % |

| GLM-5.3-Flash, steady (Triton sparse path) | 1 | 72.75 | 62.01 | 10.70 [10.41, 11.06] | +14.8 % |
| | 29 | 72.80 | 61.98 | 10.83 [10.69, 11.37] | +15.0 % |

A blocked cross-process A/B on main `72e7874fa6` (4 runs per arm, the first discarded, median of runs 2–4) agrees: 10.6–12.3 µs saved when steady, 13.0–15.8 µs when growing, 12.9–13.4 µs on the non-persistent path, with identical output hashes. At one or two builds per decode step this is under 0.1 % of a GLM-5.3 decode step, below end-to-end noise.

**e2e**, GLM-5.3-Flash (Triton sparse path), TP=2, 509 prompts in 1031 / out 509, concurrency 61, main `72e7874fa6`. The difference is within run-to-run spread, so no end-to-end speedup is claimed; per-run numbers are in the first comment.

**GSM8K** (strict-match), GLM-5.3-Flash, TP=2, main `72e7874fa6`:

commits.pr_title: [NIXL] Prepare KV transfer descriptors as NIXL 1.5 strided lists
commits.pr_body:
NIXL 1.5 accepts a compressed Nx5 descriptor list in `prep_xfer_dlist`: each `(addr, len, dev_id, stride, count)` row stands for `count` blocks of `len` bytes whose starts are `stride` bytes apart. The connector built one `(addr, len, dev_id)` row per block per region instead, so a large KV pool meant millions of descriptors materialized in NumPy and copied into NIXL at startup and again on every handshake.

Emit one strided row per region:
- `_build_fa_local`, `_build_fa_remote` and the Mamba/PLE builders return Nx5 rows. Padded blocks split by a block-size ratio get one row per block.
- Local, per-source split and remote dlists are prepared directly from the Nx5 arrays with an explicit memory type; `get_xfer_descs` is no longer used. Descriptor ids are unchanged because NIXL indexes a strided list by flat block index.
- Split handles (P_TP > D_TP) slice each row's length and address, and the REPLICATE/SPLIT flag is computed once per row from the region owning its first block, honoring per-region block counts, instead of once per block.
- Mixed DRAM/VRAM registrations split rows by memory type; the per-block maps used by the READ path are unchanged.
- The worker refuses to start with NIXL < 1.5.

The transfer path is unchanged: request descriptors are built from the same flat indices, and NIXL 1.5 already compresses flat lists internally.

## Performance

Qwen3-8B P/D on one GB300 node, NIXL 1.5.0, `main` (f2376cdc4d) vs this PR. Each decode rank has a ~1.48M-token KV pool (~3.3M per-block descriptors before this change). Method timings come from a wrapper around `register_local_xfer_handler` / `add_remote_agent`; request times are end-to-end through the toy proxy (`max_tokens=1`, ~700-token prompt). Medians of 3 rounds with alternating run order, ranges in brackets.

**Prefill TP1 → decode TP1**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Local descriptor setup (`register_local_xfer_handler`, startup) | 52 ms | 0.2 ms |
| Handshake (`add_remote_agent`) | 156 ms [153–162] | 109 ms [108–113] |
| Cold first request (includes the handshake) | 307 ms [299–341] | 259 ms [255–296] |
| Warm requests | 65–77 ms | 64–73 ms |

**Prefill TP2 → decode TP1** (decode builds per-source split handles and handshakes with two prefill ranks)

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Prefill local descriptor setup (twice the tokens per rank) | 107–112 ms | 0.1–0.2 ms |
| Handshake with first prefill rank | 2,255 ms [2,242–2,258] | 118 ms [113–118] |
| Handshake with second prefill rank | 145 ms | 42 ms |
| Cold first request | 2,656 ms [2,625–2,661] | 425 ms [415–444] |
| Warm requests | 76–89 ms | 77–99 ms |

On `main`, building the split handles looped in Python over every per-block row, costing ~2.1 s on the first handshake; it now operates on a handful of strided rows. The gain grows with KV pool size and with the prefill/decode TP ratio. The remaining ~110 ms of handshake is NIXL loading remote metadata and connecting, which this change doesn't touch. Warm request latency is unchanged, as expected, since transfer-time descriptor lookup is the same.

Ports https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55157 to current main and addresses its review feedback.

cc @iyastreb @NickLucche @tlrmchlsmth 

Used Claude Opus 5.5.
